articles.title: Adley Rutschman's three-run homer (12)
articles.summary: Adley Rutschman sends a three-run homer to right field to give the Red Sox a 4-0 lead in the bottom of the 2nd inning
articles.body:
Adley Rutschman sends a three-run homer to right field to give the Red Sox a 4-0 lead in the bottom of the 2nd inning

Swing and a shot down the right field line, near the pesky pole, and it's gone!

A three-run shot by Rutschman, an absolute laser beam, 112 off the bat.

He was ready for this one, got on top of it, banged it right off the pole.

articles.title: Jesús Luzardo gets first shutout!
articles.summary: Jesús Luzardo gets his first shutout in the Phillies' 1-0 win over the Braves
articles.body:
Jesús Luzardo gets his first shutout in the Phillies' 1-0 win over the Braves

The pitch, swing, and a fly ball, left field.

The first of his career, and the Phillies win it by a final score of one to nothing on a stunning day here at Citizens Bank Park.

He had never gotten an out in the ninth inning of a game.

Well, not only did he get a out, he got three outs.

articles.title: Jorge Martínez: "Me voy satisfecho y solo le pido al pádel del futuro que ayude a formar buenas personas"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador más laureado de la historia del pádel español anunció este martes que 2026 es su último año y repasa con MARCA Pádel su carrera deportiva.
articles.summary: El entrenador más laureado de la historia del pádel español anunció este martes que 2026 es su último año y repasa con MARCA Pádel su carrera deportiva.
articles.body: "Primero estaba él y luego llegó el pádel" es una célebre frase que define a la perfección la carrera de Jorge Martínez (Madrid, España, 1965) en el deporte de la pala como entrenador, seleccionador o formador. Como una persona del pádel. Este mismo martes ha anunciado que 2026 será su última temporada como técnico en el circuito profesional y después de muchos años en los banquillos y de haber acompañado a algunos de los grandes nombres del pádel, el madrileño afronta una nueva etapa en la que seguirá entrenando y vinculado a la competición a través de M3 Pádel Academy, pero en la que dejará de viajar de manera habitual. Inteligente y exigente, comedido y claro, y elegante y pedágogico en la crítica y el halago, Martínez ha sido el primer gran entrenador del pádel español. Su carrera ha estado basada en la formación de menores, aplicar una metodología de trabajo, en desarrollar una fórmula de éxito y crear la primera gran academia del pádel moderno. Nombres como Galán, Lebrón, Mieres, Lima, las Alayeto, Brea o el mejor Chingotto llevan su firma aunque él prefiera escudarse detrás de un concepto en desuso en el pádel: el equipo. Horas después del anuncio atiende a MARCA Pádel para charlar sobre la noticia y repasa su carrera, prolífica y exitosa, pero sacrificada y exigente, como la de un pionero que ha abierto el camino para una nueva generación que empieza ya a asomar en los banquillos del pádel. ¿Por qué ahora? No es algo que haya surgido de repente, es un tema meditado durante mucho tiempo, después de muchos años y muchas experiencias. Llega un momento en el que creo que tengo que empezar a valorar otra serie de cosas que también me apetece hacer. El circuito es muy exigente, hay muchos viajes, tensión y siempre compites por lo máximo. Creo que ha llegado el momento de parar y hacer otras cosas. ¿Recuerdas un momento concreto en el que tomaste esta decisión o ha sido un cúmulo? No hay un momento concreto. Es, como dices, una concatenación de hechos y procesos en los que vas pensando. Tú me conoces bien y sabes que hace tiempo ya decía: "Yo este año...". Pero siempre hay algún proyecto, algo pendiente que quieres hacer..., pero creo que estoy satisfecho con lo que he hecho porque me he entregado. No hay un punto de inflexión de "hasta aquí". Dejas los banquillos del circuito profesional, pero no el pádel. ¿Cuál será tu rol a partir de ahora? Voy a seguir vinculado al pádel y voy a seguir entrenando en M3. Entrenaré a jugadores de primerísimo nivel, pero no voy a viajar con ellos. Probablemente sí vaya a algún torneo elegido, acompañando a determinados jugadores y a mi equipo técnico, un poco como refuerzo, pero lo que no voy a hacer ya es el banquillo. Tengo un grupo de jóvenes y jugadores que están a punto de dar el paso que también son muy interesantes. Seguiré vinculado a la competición, pero desde otro punto de vista. En los últimos años tu nombre ha estado muy vinculado al proyecto de Federico Chingotto y Alejandro Galán. Si continúan juntos en 2027, ¿habéis pensado quién ocupará tu lugar? Desde el momento en que decido no comprometerme con la temporada siguiente, eso ya queda en sus manos. Son ellos los que tendrán que decidir cómo se van a organizar: si van a seguir con la academia o si van a buscar otra opción. Eso se lo tendrás que preguntar a ellos. De momento, el tema no está decidido. La carrera de Alejandro Galán está directamente vinculada a la tuya. ¿Cómo vivió él la noticia? Creo que Ale tiene las ideas muy claras y que sabe que todos los procesos llegan a un final y se renuevan. Creo que ya lo tenía en la cabeza y probablemente sabía que esto iba a pasar más pronto que tarde porque también he hablado con él. Ha crecido como jugador y como persona lo suficiente como para poder asumir el cambio y no creo que le vaya a suponer ningún problema. Es mucho tiempo juntos, a Galán le tienes desde menores… Llevamos 15 años juntos. El otro día hablábamos de que casi hemos construido una carrera deportiva juntos: desde que él tenía 15 años hasta los 30. Obviamente tiene que haber un cambio y una renovación, y él lo sabe. Ale es un jugador hecho, maduro, sabe muy bien lo que quiere y tiene los recursos para hacer lo que le apetezca. Él sabe que puede seguir contando conmigo para lo que quiera, pero ya desde otro punto de vista, y para él también se abre una etapa nueva. Para quienes se han incorporado al pádel en los últimos años, tu nombre está muy asociado a Galán y Chingotto, pero tu carrera es mucho más extensa. ¿Qué etapa recuerdas con especial cariño? Ha habido muchos momentos muy distintos y también hay que tener en cuenta la evolución del pádel. Las experiencias se viven de maneras diferentes y algunas son más intensas y después se diluyen porque aparece otro reto más difícil. Lo que en un momento parecía lo máximo que podías conseguir, después te das cuenta de que hay otros retos. Por supuesto, mi etapa con Lima y Mieres fue muy bonita. Estuvimos compitiendo con leyendas del pádel como Juan Martín Díaz y Fernando Belasteguín. Después llegaron las gemelas Sánchez Alayeto... Sí, la etapa con Las Gemelas también marca un antes y un después. Tuvimos la suerte de vivir juntos aquella revolución del pádel femenino con dos jugadoras absolutamente geniales, trabajadoras y diferentes. Aquellos años para mí también fue muy importante. Y llegan Lebrón, Galán, Delfi... Es que esas también han sido etapas muy bonitas porque, por ejemplo, con Delfi y Bea creo que hubo una química muy especial entre nosotros tres. También, obviamente, con Ale y Juan que salimos a luchar y a sufrir juntos hasta que se acabó la pareja y fue una etapa muy bonita. O, ahora, que lo que está pasando con Chingotto me parece que tiene un valor especial porque que conseguir sacar la mejor versión, una que el propio jugador no hubiera esperado, es algo especial y que que te lo diga tu propio jugador tiene mucho peso. Pero siempre has remarcado que el valor esta en los equipos..., ¿recuedas algún momento coral en particular? A ver, estar con la Selección Nacional fue una época muy especial. Estuve en la dirección técnica y ahí el pádel también dio un salto importante de la mano de Miguel Medina. Es algo que quizá ha pasado más desapercibido, pero que recuerdo con mucho cariño. Cuando hablas de todos esos proyectos, ¿qué importancia tiene el equipo que hay detrás? No se puede separar una cosa de la otra. Las élites salen porque detrás hay un equipo de gente que hace que todo eso sea posible. No es una cuestión de "Martínez ha hecho esto". Martínez y todos los que tiene al lado hacen que sea posible. Para mí, ese proceso ha sido clave siempre, desde menores hasta lo que vemos que es la punta del iceberg, la élite. ¿Cómo ha cambiado la gestión del talento en menores? Creo que, en la parte que nos toca en España, hay una cosa muy buena: tenemos competición de menores. Eso genera un semillero de jugadores. Hay otro factor muy importante: cada vez hay más técnicos mejor preparados y es fundamental. Si tenemos técnicos, competición y recursos para desarrollar esa competición, vamos a tener jugadores. Por dónde pasa la mejora entonces. Habrá generaciones mejores y otras algo peores, pero las bases para que esto crezca de una manera ordenada están ahí. Sí creo que se podría hacer algo más, especialmente en el seguimiento de los menores desde el ámbito federativo. Pero eso ya no depende de mí, sino de las políticas federativas y de dónde quieran invertir sus recursos. Creo que, teniendo competición y técnicos, se podría hacer un poco más de seguimiento a los jugadores. ¿Ves especialmente bien la cantera femenina? Sí. Creo que en el pádel femenino vienen jugadoras jóvenes con muchísima calidad y que van a dominar el circuito en unos años. Está Raquel Eugenio, que me parece un auténtico talentazo; Martina, que ya está ahí; Jana, que es jovencísima; Noa, Jimena... Hay muchas jugadoras jóvenes que juegan muy bien, pero muy bien. ¿Detectas demasiada premura por hacer que los jóvenes talentos lleguen rápidamente a la élite? Es que número uno solo hay uno, no pueden ser todos número uno. Y en el pádel depende muchísimo del equipo con el que cuentes. Eso es lo que marca la diferencia. Por eso siempre insisto en que, cuando hablamos de nombres individuales, que es inevitable, también es un poco injusto. Aquí hay que hablar de equipos. Yo mantengo la teoría de que el pádel es un deporte de equipo. ¿A qué te refieres? Tenemos que construir y hablar de equipos, pero no vamos a conseguirlo mientras no existan las condiciones necesarias para que los equipos puedan mantenerse y desarrollar proyectos. Eso tiene que ver también con el tipo de competición, con el ámbito federativo y con la normativa. En el caso de los jóvenes, creo que es necesario que puedan establecer proyectos y que no haya un cambio de pareja cada tres semanas o cada mes y medio. Si conseguimos eso, estaríamos hablando de otra cosa. Por tanto, más que premura, creo que lo que necesitamos son proyectos. Cuando detectas talento, hay que darle tiempo y estructura. Hemos hablado del próximo o la próxima estrella, ¿pero quién puede ser el próximo Jorge Martínez? Es muy difícil saber qué entrenador va a perder tanto tiempo como yo en el pádel (se ríe, sincero). Yo, claro, voy a tirar por mis entrenadores. Por ejemplo, Jorge de Benito me parece un entrenador que está haciendo una labor buenísima, tiene mucha implicación con los jugadores, hace seguimiento, tiene ganas de aprender... Me parece un entrenador muy a tener en cuenta. Lo mismo con David García Campos, que ya tiene mucha experiencia conmigo. Son entrenadores que tienen la personalidad y el conocimiento suficientes como para desarrollar su carrera como entrenadores de élite. Pero estoy hablando de los que conozco y de los que vivo más de cerca, no puedo hablarte de otros porque no sé qué tienen en la cabeza, cómo quieren plantear su carrera o cuál es su motivación. Lo que sí tengo es un respeto máximo por todos ellos. Si hablamos de entrenadores que ya están en la élite, ¿quiénes destacarías? Si hay que hablar de un entrenador que lleva años consiguiendo resultados en la élite, ese es Gustavo Pratto. Está llevando a los números uno desde hace años, también junto con Martín Canali, y evidentemente están ahí sus resultados. Pero si hablamos de un relevo, de futuro, te diría los que conozco y considero más interesantes y que tienen mucho futuro. Hablamos mucho de entrenadores, pero muy poco de entrenadoras. ¿Existe un problema para que las mujeres lleguen a los banquillos? Sí, es verdad. En su momento Neki hacía más banquillo, luego Marcela Ferrari, que efectivamente ha dado un paso al lado. Ahora Carolina Navarro es seleccionadora..., Creo que pueden hacerlo, pero otra cosa es que tengan las facilidades para poder desarrollarse. Como en casi todos los ámbitos deportivos, las mujeres lo tienen un poquito más difícil que nosotros. Pero hay que ponerse, tomar la decisión, apostar y tener determinación. Los entrenadores tenemos que apostar mucho. ¿Crees que la figura del entrenador está suficientemente reconocida en el pádel? Si quieres me pongo en el plano reivindicativo, aunque no me encanta (se ríe, irónicamente). Pero los entrenadores somos los grandes desconocidos de este deporte. No existimos. Nos asociamos hace un par de años para defender nuestra figura, nuestros derechos y la posibilidad de desarrollar nuestra profesión, pero no hemos avanzado mucho. Me gustaría hacer un pequeño alegato a la figura del entrenador porque creo que es muy importante en el pádel y no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Y, además, sería muy fácil empezar a mejorar, aunque solo fuera de cara a la imagen pública. Eso podría ayudar al entrenador a conseguir otros recursos y desarrollar su carrera con más desahogo. ¿A qué te refieres? Por ejemplo, en las presentaciones de Premier Padel salen los jugadores, uno detrás de otro, y luego, en una esquina, cuando ya no molestamos demasiado, aparecen los entrenadores. A mí me parece que cuando se presenta un equipo debería salir el equipo. Es una cuestión de visibilidad. Luego, si te ponen un micrófono, ahí sí que el entrenador es interesante., pero para darle visibilidad, no. Y lo mismo sucede con los premios. A los jugadores se les entrega un premio y el entrenador no existe. No hay ningún deporte de equipo en el que el entrenador no reciba el reconocimiento igual que sus jugadores. En los últimos años tenéis más altavoz, notoriedad e incluso una asociación como comentabas. Sí, pero la figura del entrenador, aunque sea con pequeñas medidas, merece ser reconocida. Y ahora que voy a dejar de hacer esto quería romper una lanza por el resto de compañeros entrenadores, que hacemos muchos esfuerzos y sacrificios para poder seguir en el circuito. Estamos aquí porque amamos la profesión y nos gusta. Como entrenador, precisamente, venís de Madrid, habéis conseguido un nuevo título y estáis más cerca que nunca del número uno. ¿Crees que Chingotto y Galán pueden acabar 2026 como números uno? Claro que sí, para eso nos levantamos entrenamos y competimos cada día. Desde el primer día creo que podemos ser número uno. No hay ninguna duda. Nosotros vamos a por el número uno. Dicho así puede parecer un poco soberbio, pero es nuestro objetivo final. Ahora bien, sabemos que para ser número uno primero hay que levantarse, entrenar cada día a muerte, jugar el primer partido, ganar el primer punto, después el siguiente..., descansar y volver a empezar. Hay que ir etapa a etapa, pasito a pasito, hasta que al final llegas a la meta. ¿Cómo se consigue mantener viva la llama en un proceso ya de tres años? La meta es esa, obviamente, pero siempre hemos tenido claro que el camino tiene que ser poco a poco. Creo que tengo un equipo bastante humilde en ese sentido y que solo piensa en dar el máximo en cada punto. Y creo que tanto Chingotto como Galán lo tienen grabado a fuego. A veces está mejor uno y otras veces está mejor el otro, pero esa sintonía que hay entre ellos creo que les está permitiendo superar situaciones que quizá serían insalvables en otro equipo. Y ya estamos a mitad de año y seguimos ahí. Has sido número uno con Lima y Mieres, con las gemelas, con Lebrón y Galán, con Brea. ¿Sería conseguirlo ahora con Chingotto y Galán el mayor hito de tu carrera? No sé si sería el mayor, porque creo que los hitos dependen del momento y de las circunstancias. Cuando te has cruzado con Belasteguín y Juan Martín Díaz, por ejemplo, y has conseguido estar por delante aunque fuera durante una semana o por un ajuste del calendario, tiene muchísimo mérito (se ríe). También era un hito muy importante para Delfi y para el pádel argentino ser número uno y se consiguió... ¿Sería este el más importante? Sería muy importante, sí, pero no sé si el más importante. No creo que haya uno por encima de otro. No lo valoraría más que los demás. Una de las espinitas que podría quedar es Bea González. Estuvisteis muy cerca de conseguir el número uno con ella y Delfi. ¿No haberlo logrado es algo que se queda en el debe? No, no se me queda en el debe. La experiencia que tuve con Bea y con Delfi fue tan bonita que el número del ranking queda en un segundo plano. Se queda muy lejos de lo que para mí significó la complicidad con aquella pareja. Te diría que fue de las parejas con las que más he disfrutado en una competición. Recuerdo un partido en Madrid que ganamos a Paula y Ari con el partido prácticamente perdido... Fue la final del Madrid P1 de 2023. Exacto, de la fecha no me acuerdo, pero sí del remate que pegó Paula con la punta cuando tenían el partido ganado y acabamos remontando. Esa experiencia, para mí, fue tan bonita y tan emocionante que valió un número uno en mi cabeza y en mi corazón. Por eso no se me queda en el debe. También has vivido otros momentos muy especiales, como el FIP World Champhionships del año pasado. Sí, claro, ganar el Mundial por parejas también es un hito. No es un número uno, pero es un campeonato del mundo y eso tampoco es poca cosa. Es un título y los títulos tienen muchísimo mérito. Ser campeón del mundo implica una dosis de competición extra que no está al alcance de cualquiera. También recuerdo el Mundial que ganaron Fernando Poggi y Cristian Gutiérrez frente a jugadores como Juan Martín y Belasteguín que fue otro momento que tengo en la retina. Son momentos muy bonitos. ¿Dónde ves el pádel dentro de 10 o 15 años? Lo veo en lo más alto. Creo que va a ser, como ya lo es, un deporte a nivel mundial, con un circuito muy potente. Ya existe una industria alrededor del deporte y eso es muy importante para que pueda desarrollarse. La parte de comunicación también está creciendo mucho y cada vez mejor. Soy muy optimista con el desarrollo del pádel. ¿Ha mejorado mucho los últimos años, pero desde dentro dónde se ven los márgenes de crecimiento? Sí creo que hay algunas cosas que, a nivel organizativo, tienen que mejorar para que el deporte crezca de una manera más ordenada y tenga cabida mucha más gente. Podemos mejorar desde la organización de los torneos, especialmente en la parte técnica, y ceo que hacer un circuito con unos torneos en los que los jugadores puedan establecer una estrategia le daría mucha más visibilidad al deporte y a muchos más jugadores. Eso puede ser una de las claves para que todo lo que hay debajo, la parte amateur, la producción, las ventas..., también mejore. Hay una responsabilidad grande en conseguir una competición con personalidad propia y que sirva para que el aficionado se relacione todavía más con el pádel. En varios momentos de tu carrera has comentado que el público que hay en el pádel es algo muy especial... Es que yo sigo alucinando cuando voy a los estadios. Este fin de semana, por ejemplo, en Madrid fue espectacular. La cantidad de gente que fue, cómo vibró... La gente participa del espectáculo, grita, aplaude, anima a uno y al contrario. Anima a los cuatro. Eso no pasa en ningún deporte. La gente disfruta del espectáculo y eso es maravilloso. En otros deportes eres de tu equipo, pero aquí la gente es del pádel. Aquí la gente grita por Chingotto en un lado y dos minutos después está gritando por Coki. Eso me parece maravilloso y no se puede perder. Si conseguimos que, a nivel normativo, el deporte crezca de una manera ordenada y lógica, tenemos pádel para aburrir. Si pudieras pedir un deseo deportivo, ¿qué pedirías? Es una pregunta muy difícil. No sabría decirte. No tengo un deseo concreto que no se haya cumplido. Hay muchas cosas que no se han cumplido, pero entiendo que no se han cumplido porque quizá no tenían que cumplirse. Si tengo que desear algo para el pádel, es que consigamos que sea un deporte que realmente sirva para formar y que los jugadores que entren a jugar al pádel sean mejores como personas. Que los chavales aprendan a ser mejores, a tener más valores a través del pádel. Eso es, para mí, lo único que nuestro deporte debería tener un poco más: que hubiera más compromiso y más valores, y que los chavales pudieran educarse a través de los valores del pádel. El equipo, el compañerismo, el respeto... Para mí, ese sería el mayor deseo que le pediría al deporte. Y si, para acabar, tuvieras que definir tu carrera... Pues que me siento bien conmigo mismo. Creo que he sido honesto y leal conmigo. Me gusta lo que hago y disfruto y he disfrutado muchísimo de ello. Creo que ha sido una carrera deportiva bonita y buena. Me voy satisfecho.

articles.title: Manu Bhaker suffers another personal loss; grandmother Daya Kaur passes away in Rohtak
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker suffered another personal setback on Tuesday as her 84-year-old grandmother, Daya Kaur, passed away at a priv.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker suffered another personal setback on Tuesday as her 84-year-old grandmother, Daya Kaur, passed away at a private hospital in Rohtak.Daya Kaur had been admitted to the hospital after experiencing chest pain and was also dealing with age-related health complications. She shared a close bond with Manu and remained one of her biggest sources of affection and support.The grief comes at a difficult time for Manu, who is already coping with the recent setback involving her coach Jaspal Rana. The shooter was undergoing training in Bhopal as part of her preparations for the Asian Games when she received news of her grandmother's demise. She immediately left for her native village.Manu's family was with Daya Kaur during her final hours. Her mother was in Bhopal with Manu, while her father, Mahendra Bhaker, was in Ahmedabad. Other family members were also away, while her aunt was present at the hospital.Daya Kaur had followed Manu's journey closely, including her historic performance at the Paris Olympics, where Manu became the first Indian athlete since independence to win two medals at a single edition of the Games. She had watched her granddaughter's events from her village and celebrated her success with immense pride.For Manu, the loss is deeply personal. Family members recall the special bond between the two, with Daya Kaur often pampering her granddaughter and feeding her traditional homemade choorma.Manu's shooting commitments are now temporarily on hold as she returns home to be with her family. The Indian shooting team is scheduled to leave on Sept 15.Daya Kaur's last rites will be performed at her native village on Wednesday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jessica Pegula beats Emma Navarro to set up Sabalenka semifinal at US Open
articles.summary: Pegula claims a 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 win over Navarro in an all-American quarterfinal and will face Sabalenka on Thursday.
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula has booked a third straight US Open face-off with Aryna Sabalenka , grinding out a 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 win over Emma Navarro to set up a semifinal clash with the two-time defending champion and the world’s top-ranked women’s player.

Third-seeded Pegula needed two hours and 20 minutes to get past Navarro on Tuesday, recovering from an early break in the third set of a tense baseline battle on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

“It was really tough,” Pegula said after a match featuring nine breaks of serve. “It was physical, humid. I wasn’t exactly serving my best, and I was fighting a lot of demons out there today.”

Pegula improved to 5-0 against Navarro, a former world number eight who is on the rise after an extended break to focus on health issues, winning her first title in more than a year at Strasbourg in May.

Pegula, who has won two titles this year, is among the trio of players who arrived at Flushing Meadows with a chance to supplant Sabalenka atop the world rankings in New York.

Sabalenka beat Pegula in the 2024 final in Flushing Meadows and beat her again in the semis last year on the way to a second crown.

The 32-year-old would have to go all the way to a first major title to have a shot at claiming the top spot.

But the number one issue could be moot by the time Pegula and Sabalenka square-off on Thursday.

Second-ranked Elena Rybakina can seize the top spot regardless of other results with a win over China’s Zheng Qinwen in their quarterfinal on Wednesday.

articles.title: Asian Games host city hit by floods, official says 'we are not worried'
articles.summary: Off the field News: Athletes who arrived early for the Asian Games in Nagoya were safe after heavy rain caused flooding across parts of the central Japanese city, Mayor I.
articles.body: Athletes who arrived early for the Asian Games in Nagoya were safe after heavy rain caused flooding across parts of the central Japanese city, Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa said on Wednesday.The Asian Games are scheduled to begin on September 19 in Nagoya and surrounding areas and will continue until October 4. Hirosawa said the flooding had not affected the venues and that the event would go ahead as planned.“We are not worried about the conditions of the venues and we believe there is no problem holding the Asian Games as planned,” Hirosawa said, s quoted by news agncy Associated Press.More than 11,000 athletes from 45 countries and regions in Asia are expected to take part in the Games. That is more than the 10,700 athletes who competed at the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris.The previous edition of the Asian Games was held three years ago in Hangzhou, China.Hirosawa said around 400 athletes and staff staying in converted shipping containers, which have been remodelled as temporary housing units for the Asian Games, were briefly moved to higher ground during the heavy rain.There were also several reports of leaking roofs, but Hirosawa said there was no more serious damage around the dozens of Games venues.Record rainfall hit parts of Nagoya on Tuesday, flooding dozens of roads and homes and leaving pedestrians and vehicles stranded. Bus and subway services in the city were also temporarily suspended, the mayor said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asian Games athletes forced to evacuate amid record rainfall in Japan
articles.summary: Rainwater leaked into competition venues a day before some preopening ceremony competitions beginning on Thursday.
articles.body:
Hundreds of Asian Games athletes in Japan were briefly evacuated from their accommodation as record rainfall lashed host city Nagoya, officials have said.

About 104mm (4 inches) of rain fell in an hour in Nagoya on Tuesday, prompting municipal officials to issue an evacuation order for parts of the city.

articles.title: Team calls Chinese race organizers ‘grossly negligent’ in conduct around fiery crash
articles.summary: A car racing team whose injured driver was rescued by another competitor after a horrific crash in Shanghai on Saturday has called the organizers “grossly negligent in the safety response” and said it is withdrawing from future events in China.
articles.body: A car racing team whose injured driver was rescued by another competitor after a horrific crash in Shanghai on Saturday has called the organizers “grossly negligent in the safety response” and said it is withdrawing from future events in China. The car of British driver Ollie Millroy exploded into flames in a GT race at the Shanghai International Circuit. And it was another driver, Loek Hartog, who stopped his car and, armed with a fire extinguisher, pulled Millroy out of the burning wreckage. “I am still alive tonight, entirely thanks to one man. Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshals or fire crews in sight and risked his own life to get me out of the car,” Millroy wrote on his Instagram account. “I don’t remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and 1 hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life.” Hartog responded with humility to the praise. “You have nothing to thank me for,” he said. “I wish to live in a world where this would not be considered as bravery — but as the instinct of others, too. I am so grateful to have been at the place I needed to be.” According to his Instagram account, Millroy sustained six broken ribs, a broken collarbone, a broken hand, and a punctured lung. He underwent a four-hour operation in a Shanghai hospital to insert plates and screws into the broken bones. Doctors also inserted a drain line into his abdomen to release gas and fluid leaking from his lung. Millroy’s team, AAI Motorsports, in a long statement was scathing about the conduct of Chinese organizers. “The event organizer was grossly negligent in its emergency response and safety rescue arrangements, with serious deficiencies in the rescue response that nearly resulted in a tragedy,” the team wrote. “Even more outrageously, during the live broadcast of the accident, event staff failed to verify the on-site situation and hastily reported that the driver had left the wrecked vehicle on his own. In fact, the driver of our No. 91 car was pulled out of the burning car by Loek Hartog, driver of the No. 79 car of Phantom Team who risked his own life to carry out the rescue.” AAI Motorsports called for a “comprehensive investigation” and public disclosure around the accident, track safety, and the emergency response. It said it would withdraw from all GT events in China until its demands were met. “We will not return until the event organizing committee conducts a comprehensive, independent and transparent investigation into every aspect of the incident, including the failures in the rescue response, and provides our team with an official response.” In a statement, event organizers apologized for the “incident and the distress” it caused and offered “sincere sympathy” to the injured driver. But organizers also defended some of the conduct. “According to our preliminary review, the event’s overall staffing and resources met the standards required for a national-level motorsport event, although there remains room for improvement in detailed operational management,” organizers wrote. “We will conduct a further review and investigation into the accident and develop more comprehensive plans to address shortcomings in race organization, support arrangements, emergency response, rescue operations and medical services.”

articles.title: Should Leeds have signed a back-up striker?
articles.summary: Derek asked me why Leeds have not signed a striker to deputise for Dominic Calvert-Lewin and wonders if the Leeds recruitment team have been short sighted....
articles.body:
Some of you have been in touch using our Ask Me Anything form on Leeds United.

Derek asked me why Leeds have not signed a striker to deputise for Dominic Calvert-Lewin and wonders if the Leeds recruitment team have been short sighted.

I can say I don't think it was for the lack of trying Derek. Daniel Farke was clear that he wanted to add two or three senior and proven players to his attack. Harry Wilson obviously came in while Mikhailo Mudryk did not, so the latter slot was replaced with the potential of Jean-Matteo Bahoya. When it comes to another centre-forward I really think it comes down to affordability of a player who can improve the squad.

Ipswich Town paid £20m for Burnley 's Zian Fleming which seems a reasonable price for a 28-year-old with Premier League experience. However, he will probably start for them whereas at United he would be third choice. Be honest, in this summer's market were you able to buy a top quality striker for anything near a sensible price?

Also, the new Squad Cost Ratio parameters make it slightly more difficult for Leeds United in the short term to spend on signings after shelling out big fees for James Trafford and Tarik Muharemovic , whilst admittedly selling Pascal Struijk . You also have to factor in the cost of the improved contracts for senior players like Ethan Ampadu , Joe Rodon and Jayden Bogle and the lift in the salary level.

Ask Me Anything is a service dedicated to answering your questions.

We want to reward your time by telling you things you do not know and reminding you of things you do.

articles.title: Stacy’s Streamers: Four Players to Start in Week 1
articles.summary: Stacy Perez highlights one player at each position who is worth streaming in Week 1.
articles.body:
Not every Week 1 lineup decision is a no-brainer. Whether you're working around a tough matchup, trying to fill a roster hole or just looking for a little upside, these four players are worth a look. They may not be automatic starts every week, but the opportunity is there this week.

Quarterback: Jared Goff ‐ Lions vs. Saints

Why I like him: Despite finishing each of the last few seasons with top-10 fantasy production, Goff continues to be drafted well outside that range. His ADP this season has him coming off the board around QB16 or QB17, which makes him exactly the kind of player worth considering as a Week 1 streamer.

Goff has also historically been a better quarterback indoors than outdoors, and that trend continued in 2025 with a higher completion percentage and passer rating in dome games. Detroit may be opening the season on the road, but the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans still gives Goff the benefit of playing indoors.

The matchup is appealing as well. The Saints gave quarterbacks the second-most time to throw in the NFL last season, an especially important advantage for a traditional pocket passer like Goff, who isn't going to create much extra time with his legs. New Orleans has made some improvements to its pass defense, but there is still enough here to make Goff a very viable Week 1 starter.

The play: Goff is firmly in the Week 1 starter conversation.

Running Back: Marshawn Lloyd ‐ Packers vs. Vikings

Why I like him: Lloyd has been climbing draft boards since Josh Jacobs was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List, sidelining him for the foreseeable future. Green Bay added Kaleb Johnson for depth, but Lloyd is expected to handle the lead role until Jacobs returns. That kind of opportunity is hard to ignore, and the projected volume alone puts Lloyd firmly in the starting conversation.

The matchup helps, too. Green Bay opens the season against division rival Minnesota, which has a run defense with some question marks entering the season. Brian Flores' defense ranked 21st in rushing yards allowed per game last season, and opponents ran the ball against the Vikings 51.6% of the time, the highest rate in the NFL. For a back expected to see a healthy workload, that gives Lloyd a very appealing Week 1 setup.

The play: Lloyd is easily a RB2 in lineups this week.

Wide Receiver: Quentin Johnston ‐ Chargers vs. Cardinals

Why I like him: Plenty of excitement has surrounded new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and what his offense could mean for the Chargers' playmakers this season. Johnston has been one of the bigger names in that conversation, especially after showing real improvement in 2025. McDaniel has also specifically praised Johnston's growth during spring workouts, adding even more reason for optimism heading into Week 1.

The opportunity is there, too. Keenan Allen's departure leaves more than 100 targets up for grabs in this offense, and Johnston has a clear path to a meaningful share of them. After taking a step forward last season, he enters 2026 with a chance to turn that progress into a much larger role.

Arizona makes for an appealing opening matchup. The Cardinals allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers last season, surrendering 230 passing yards and 31 passing touchdowns. Even with some offseason changes, expectations for this defense remain modest, making Johnston an intriguing upside play to open the season.

The play: Johnston offers WR3/Flex upside with the potential for a much bigger Week 1 if his expanded role shows up right away.

Tight End: Dalton Kincaid ‐ Bills vs. Texans

Why I like him: The Texans have one of the best defenses in football, if not the best, so fantasy managers should naturally temper expectations for players facing a unit led by Will Anderson Jr. and Derek Stingley Jr. However, before you cross Kincaid off the list entirely, the matchup deserves a closer look.

Kincaid enters the season fully healthy and is coming off the best fantasy season of his career, averaging 10.5 fantasy points per game. More importantly for Week 1, tight end may be the softest spot in an otherwise dominant Houston defense. The Texans allowed 12.6 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends last season.

Houston will likely devote plenty of attention to taking away Buffalo's biggest offensive threats, including James Cook and DJ Moore. That could leave Kincaid as one of Josh Allen's more dependable options underneath and over the middle, giving him a path to useful fantasy production even in a difficult matchup.

The play: Kincaid is a viable TE1 streamer in Week 1 despite the intimidating matchup.

As always with streamers, the goal is not to find the biggest name. It's to find the right opportunity for the week in front of you. Week 1 is finally here, and it feels good to be back. Let's go get those wins!

It's been a busy start to the 2026-27 campaign for Brighton and Fabian Hurzeler must now begin to prepare for a packed schedule of domestic and European football.

Although the Seagulls will wait until October for their Conference League league phase to start, Hurzeler's side has endured a flurry of mixed results in their opening five games of the season.

After a bruising 4-3 loss at Stamford Bridge to transfer-foes Chelsea , Brighton were lucky to escape with a 1-1 draw at home to Leeds .

Former Seagulls midfielder Warren Aspinall told BBC Radio Sussex's Albion Unlimited podcast Leeds "should have scored more" when they were dominating the early stages of the game.

"We always say when teams are on top, punish the opposition. We got going in the last half an hour, and we were the better team," said Aspinall.

Brighton had a stronghold of 67.1% possession throughout the game, and attempted a total of 522 passes compared to Leeds' 252.

Aspinall added: "I don't think it is possession, it is the energy, then move the ball with a purpose instead of going sideways and back. You're never going to hurt anybody doing that."

A Luka Vuskovic goal salvaged a point for Brighton and the equaliser will be deemed extremely valuable as Hurzeler's side have the most injuries of any Premier League team at this stage of the season.

As it stands, Brighton have 10 players ruled out by injury, with the likes of Georginio Rutter , Jack Hinshelwood and Kaoru Mitoma all unavailable.

articles.title: Cowboys Issued Strong Josh Sweat Take Amid 49ers Speculation
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers need more of a running mate to go along with Nick Bosa. Moreover, the Niners shouldn’t put all their hopes of sacking the quarterback...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers need more of a running mate to go along with Nick Bosa. Moreover, the Niners shouldn't put all their hopes of sacking the quarterback on Bosa, given his injury history; he's dealt with tendinitis during training camp and the preseason.

As a result, the Niners could use the first two months of the season to monitor veteran pass rushers who could be available around the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Recently, KNBR's Larry Krueger stated that Arizona Cardinals' Josh Sweat should be a name the 49ers pursue.

It's likely the Cardinals, who are in a rebuild, will be sellers at the deadline, and Sweat could be available at the right price. For Jerry Trotta of FanSided, it's the Dallas Cowboys, not the 49ers, who make sense for Sweat. As part of his trade pitch, he sees the Cowboys sending a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 third-round pick for Sweat.

"If traded, Sweat should fetch a fraction of what [Maxx] Crosby does. A third-round pick and a Day 3 selection may be rich, but Jones may have to overpay a smidge if the 29-year-old has a robust market," Trotta wrote in a Sept. 8 article. "That should be the case, as he's been remarkably consistent and durable."

Why Cowboys Make Sense for Cardinals' Josh Sweat

Last season, Sweat played 540 defensive snaps for the Cardinals, leading to a 74.2 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, he generated 47 total pressures, 12 sacks, 29 hurries, and six QB hits. Sweat also registered three forced fumbles, 20 stops, and 11 solo tackles.

Moreover, Trotta noted why trading Sweat to the Cowboys makes sense rather than trading him elsewhere to a team like the 49ers.

"A former star for Vic Fangio, Sweat would be a seamless fit in a Christian Parker scheme that's expected to be an extension of Fangio's," Trotta added in his article. "He'd also walk into a locker room full of familiar faces, including Klayton Adams, Ryan Smith, Jalen Thompson and Emari Demercado."

Analyst Would Back 49ers In Potential Trade for Maxx Crosby

If San Francisco wanted to take a home run swing in a midseason trade, NFL analyst Brian Baldinger would support an aggressive move by pursuing Las Vegas Raiders star Maxx Crosby .

"You're in an arms race with the Rams right now," Baldinger said in a Sept. 1 appearance on 95.7 The Game . "This is a military arms race trying to keep up. I don't know that Maxx Crosby is available or could be had. I have no idea.

"All I know is I was at the Sack Summit out in Las Vegas a month ago, and nobody could beat him off the line of scrimmage. Everybody challenged him. Jared Verse , pick a guy that was out there. Nobody could beat him off the ball. Nobody. He won it."

Last season with the Raiders, Crosby played 935 total snaps on defense, leading to a 79.7 overall PFF defensive grade . The veteran pass rusher generated 53 total pressures, 10 sacks, 31 hurries, 12 QB hits, and a forced fumble. Meanwhile, against the run, he recorded 46 solo tackles.

Linda Cohn is back with another take on A'ja Wilson and Caitlin Clark.

In light of A'ja Wilson's absence from Team USA for the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, sports analyst Linda Cohn insinuated that she was insecure about Caitlin Clark.

Cohn's comments weren't received well, as fans of both stars called her out for starting an unnecessary debate as Wilson missed the tournament due to injury.

Linda Cohn clarifies her A'ja Wilson, Caitlin Clark comments

Following the ruthless reaction from WNBA fans, Cohn explained her point during the latest episode of her show on YouTube.

"When I'm watching the best player in the world doing that, playing those minutes, putting up those numbers, collecting Player of the Week and Player of the Month honors, and then suddenly she decided without any public announcement that she's not going to the World Cup just a couple of days before the team boards the plane, I'm going to ask questions," Cohn said.

She added, "I went right to the source, USA Basketball. It cited health reasons, no details given. I was curious. … So why didn't USA Basketball know about it? They detailed Kelsey Plum's injury but not A'ja's. I was just asking questions."

To be fair, Cohn's explanation makes sense, but she could have done it without bringing Clark into the conversation.

Suggesting that Wilson decided to sit out of the tournament to avoid being overshadowed by Clark is what made fans angry. It will be interesting to see if Cohn's explanation will take the heat off her or if the damage is beyond repair.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers reveals the remarkable Mike Tomlin trait that made him want to play for Steelers
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has revealed the remarkable Mike Tomlin trait that helped convince him to play for the Pittsburgh Steelers, praising the former head coach for...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has revealed the remarkable Mike Tomlin trait that helped convince him to play for the Pittsburgh Steelers , praising the former head coach for remembering personal details about virtually every player in the organisation.

Rodgers opened up about Tomlin during a new episode of the Not Just Football with Cam Heyward podcast, explaining why the longtime Steelers coach left such a strong impression on him.

Tomlin's ability to connect with players went beyond what happened on the field. Rodgers said the coach knew the stories behind the people on his roster and made a point of remembering the details they shared with him.

Aaron Rodgers explains why Mike Tomlin stood out from other coaches

Rodgers was particularly impressed by how Tomlin treated players as individuals rather than simply members of a 90-man roster.

"Every call, which was probably once a week or once every five days, he remembered names. He asked about the people and how they were doing. I was really touched by the level of attention."

That personal connection continued whenever Tomlin discussed members of his team.

"Then it carried over. When he talked about the guys, he knew everybody. Not just knew them by their name, there's 90 guys on the roster, but he knew everybody's story."

Rodgers said that level of care was a major reason he wanted to play for Tomlin.

"I thought that was such an awesome thing that's just not replicated around the league, and I'm sure not in other sports. Just such an intimate knowledge of the guys and what made them tick. That's why I really wanted to play for him, because you knew Mike T cared about us."

The veteran quarterback also highlighted another side of Tomlin's personality, describing his charisma in remarkably strong terms.

"He also is super charismatic. I've been around a few charismatic people in my life, and I would put him on the same level as meeting Michael Jordan or Kobe Bryant."

Rodgers' comments underline the relationship Tomlin built with his players during his time in Pittsburgh. That connection clearly mattered to Rodgers when he chose to join the Steelers, and it remains one of the traits he remembers most fondly about his former coach.

articles.title: Lewis Hall Extends His Contract At Newcastle Until 2031
articles.summary: The rising England international cements his future on Tyneside, rewarding the Magpies' faith after evolving from a promising loanee into a vital fixture of...
articles.body:
Lewis Hall has committed his long-term future to Newcastle United by signing a new contract that will keep him at St James' Park until 2031.

The new deal represents a significant show of faith in the England international, who has continued to establish himself as an important part of Newcastle's squad since making his move to the club.

Hall initially joined Newcastle from Chelsea , spending the early part of his career adapting to a new environment and competing for a place within Eddie Howe's squad. What began as a loan move eventually became a permanent transfer, and the left-back has since developed into a player capable of playing an increasingly important role for the Magpies.

His progress has been particularly notable given the competition for places at Newcastle . Hall has had to demonstrate his ability to contribute both defensively and in possession, while also adapting to the demands of playing regularly at the highest level.

The 21-year-old's development has also seen him break into the England setup, further underlining the progress he has made since arriving on Tyneside.

The decision to extend Hall's contract through to 2031 provides Newcastle with further long-term security around a player they clearly see as an important part of their future. Rather than allowing uncertainty to develop around his situation, the club have moved to reward his development and ensure one of their promising young players remains tied down for the foreseeable future.

For Hall, the new agreement is another major milestone in what has been an impressive rise.

There have been moments during his Newcastle career when his path to regular first-team football has not been straightforward. Injuries and competition for places have tested his patience, but his performances have increasingly demonstrated why Newcastle were so keen to secure his services permanently.

The defender has shown versatility, technical ability and a willingness to take responsibility in possession. Those qualities fit the profile of the modern full-back, while his age means there remains significant scope for further improvement.

Newcastle's decision to hand Hall a contract running until 2031 also reflects the club's wider approach to building a squad capable of competing domestically and in Europe over the long term.

With Hall now committed to Newcastle for another five seasons beyond the current campaign, the club can continue to develop him without the immediate concern of his contract situation.

For supporters, the extension should be viewed as another positive piece of business. Hall has already shown flashes of the player he can become, and there is a growing belief that his best years are still ahead of him.

The challenge now will be for Hall to continue his upward trajectory and cement himself as Newcastle's long-term first-choice option on the left side of defence.

After overcoming setbacks and adapting to the demands of life at St James' Park, Hall has been rewarded with a contract that demonstrates Newcastle's belief in his potential.

With his future secured until 2031, attention can now turn towards what could be the next stage of his development on Tyneside.

Newcastle have made it clear that Lewis Hall is part of their long-term plans, and the defender now has the opportunity to repay that faith by becoming an established figure in the Magpies' first team for years to come.

articles.title: Commanders vs. Eagles: 5 things to know for Week 1
articles.summary: Here are five things to know for Sunday's Week 1 matchup between the Commanders and Eagles.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is finally here. The season officially begins on Wednesday, when the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch. The Washington Commanders begin their season on Sunday, as they head up I-95 to face the two-time defending NFC East champion Philadelphia Eagles .

The Eagles became the first NFC East team in over 20 years to win back-to-back division titles last season. Philadelphia's season came to an end in the NFC Wild Card round, as the Eagles fell to the San Francisco 49ers 23-19.

The Commanders are coming off a disappointing 5-12 season — one year after a shocking run to the NFC Championship Game, where they fell to the Eagles.

Here are five things to know about the Week 1 matchup between the two longtime NFC East rivals.

The Commanders and Eagles have opened the season in Philadelphia five previous times. Washington holds a 3-2 edge in those five previous road Week 1 meetings in Philly. The last time the Commanders opened a season in Philadelphia was in 2019. The Eagles won, 32-27, but that was Terry McLaurin 's first career NFL game, when he caught five passes for 125 yards and a touchdown. Quarterback Case Keenum missed a wide-open McLaurin on another potential touchdown.

Sunday's game will be the 12th time that Philadelphia and Washington meet in Week 1. The Commanders hold a 6-5 edge, including winning the last meeting in 2020, 27-17. Dwayne Haskins started under center for Washington and completed 17 of 31 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown. Peyton Barber scored two rushing touchdowns on that day, while McLaurin led the team with five receptions for 61 yards.

Commanders and Eagles are tied up in Philadelphia

Washington and Philadelphia have met 90 times in the City of Brotherly Love. Each team has won 44 games, and they have tied twice. They last met in Week 18 in January, when the Commanders defeated the Eagles 24-17 with third-string quarterback Josh Johnson under center. It was a battle of backups, as Philadelphia rested its starters, while Washington had a good portion of its original starting lineup on injured reserve.

No A.J. Brown for the first time since 2021

The Eagles traded away star wide receiver A.J. Brown this offseason. That should make Washington fans happy. In seven career games vs. the Commanders, Brown caught 45 passes for 654 yards and six touchdowns. He was dominant against any combination of Washington cornerbacks over the past four years. DeVonta Smith ascends into the No. 1 role, and he, too, has enjoyed some success against the Commanders.

Daniels didn't play in either of last season's matchups, but he did face the Eagles three times in 2024, including the NFC Championship Game. In two regular-season meetings, Daniels has completed 46 of his 71 passing attempts (65%) for 449 yards with six touchdowns and three interceptions. He also rushed for 81 yards in that second meeting, in which he passed for a career-high five touchdowns and led the Commanders to an impressive come-from-behind win. Daniels also played well against Philadelphia in the NFC Championship, but fumbles by Austin Ekeler and Dyami Brown allowed the game to get out of hand.

articles.title: ‘Not going anywhere…’ Joe Burrow seemingly commits future to Cincinnati Bengals ahead of 2026 season
articles.summary: Joe Burrow is here to stay with the Cincinnati Bengals, as he looks to take the team back to the Super Bowl for the first time in five years. Burrow led the...
articles.body:
Joe Burrow is here to stay with the Cincinnati Bengals, as he looks to take the team back to the Super Bowl for the first time in five years.

Burrow led the Bengals to the Super Bowl in 2022, where they eventually came up short against the Los Angeles Rams and Matthew Stafford.

Since then, the Bengals have missed the playoffs for three straight years, and only reached the AFC Championship game once, losing to eventual champions Kansas City Chiefs in 2023.

Joe Burrow eyeing long-term future with Cincinnati Bengals with Super Bowl dreams

Speaking to Bengals.com , Joe Burrow confirmed that he has no desire to leave the Cincinnati Bengals any time soon.

He wants to help the team develop a championship mindset and lead the team back to glory while representing all their fans well.

"I'm here for the long haul. I'm not going anywhere. I'm just trying to bring a now-or-never mentality to the day-by-day process.

"If you're not, what are you doing? Attack the day with a championship mindset. The rest will take care of itself.

"I'm just really proud to be quarterback of the Bengals. I'm happy to be here. I'm proud to represent the city of Cincinnati, state of Ohio, the Brown family. I'm just proud and I want to make everybody else proud, too."

Burrow has also taken on more of a leadership role with the team during the training camp, trying to lead the team on all fronts.

"I've been pushed to do that in the past. Not necessarily here, but just in my football life," Burrow said.

"I've tried it before, and it's not really for me. But as I've grown and matured, I just think you have to be able to do it at some points, and you can't be so bad at it when you have to do it."

The Bengals will have to overcome a tough AFC North group, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers also trying to reach the Super Bowl this year.

If Burrow can allow the Bengals to top the group, they will have a strong chance of making a big run in the playoffs.

articles.title: Verstappen sees an opportunity in Madrid to get Red Bull to the front quickly
articles.summary: Red Bull Racing heads to the Spanish Grand Prix with a fair bit of uncertainty. Max Verstappen still took a podium in Monza, but the new circuit in Madrid ma...
articles.body:
Red Bull Racing heads to the Spanish Grand Prix with a fair bit of uncertainty. Max Verstappen still took a podium in Monza, but the new circuit in Madrid makes it hard to gauge where the RB22 will stand this coming weekend. On the other hand, the Dutchman also sees opportunities in the unknown factors awaiting him.

Verstappen had a mixed weekend in Italy, but ultimately managed to get the most out of his Red Bull. The four-time world champion finished third, keeping the McLarens and Ferraris behind him. Still, that result offers few guarantees for Madrid. The Madring is completely new for all Formula 1 teams except Ferrari, and Verstappen has only experienced the circuit in the simulator so far.

"It was a great result for us in Monza and we really maximized our performance there to secure a podium," Verstappen reflects. "Looking ahead to Madrid, it's hard to predict how we'll perform there. We've practiced on the simulator and it seems like a more challenging track to drive, as with most street circuits, especially because there are so many tricky corners."

The first free practice will therefore feature a packed program for Verstappen. A lot of data needs to be gathered to set up the car for the rest of the weekend. "We'll also have to assess how much grip there is on Friday and build from there. Practice will be important to learn as much as possible before qualifying begins," Verstappen continues. Still, he also sees an opportunity for Red Bull. "That said, it's a new circuit for everyone and hopefully we can hit the ground running and make a strong start."

Max Verstappen took a podium in Monza - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool

Teammate Liam Lawson also isn't quite sure what to expect from Red Bull in Madrid. The 24-year-old will line up alongside Verstappen again, as Isack Hadjar is not yet fit enough to return behind the wheel. The New Zealander likewise emphasizes that the simulator only tells part of the story. Only during first practice will it become clear how well the car actually suits the new circuit.

In principle, everyone is in the same boat. "Madrid will be an interesting weekend for everyone. So far we've only driven the track in the simulator, so first practice will tell us a lot about where we really stand," Lawson says. "It's a unique circuit and the banked corner should make it interesting." For him, it's also a chance to come back stronger after Monza. The weekend in Italy was somewhat challenging.

"Monza was a tough weekend from the start, because the engine change immediately put us on the back foot. That made it difficult to fully show what we were capable of," Lawson explains. "The positive is that we found good pace over the course of the weekend. That gives us confidence heading into Madrid."

The weather also looks set to be an important factor during Madrid's debut weekend. It's expected to stay dry and sunny, with temperatures rising from around 31 degrees on Friday to 33 degrees on Sunday. First practice starts on Friday at 1:30 p.m. You can find the full schedule here.

articles.title: Liverpool take first steps towards move for Newcastle star
articles.summary: Liverpool have reportedly taken the first steps towards a move for a Newcastle United star. A blockbuster deal on the way?Liverpool are already planning ahea...
articles.body:
Liverpool have reportedly taken the first steps towards a move for a Newcastle United star. A blockbuster deal on the way?

Liverpool are already planning ahead in their transfer plans. The Reds may only just have come out of the summer window but it's plain to all that work needs to be done.

And that's despite Richard Hughes leaving as sporting director. He's joined Al-Hilal, leaving Liverpool short and lacking on a proper overseer right now. Still, those who remain have got to figure out the January strategy.

That's not simple. Liverpool need players all over the place, with long-term doubts at centre-back, right-back, left-back, goalkeeper, centre-midfield, and on the right wing.

Centre-back is a particularly notable one. Liverpool have five options in their senior squad but only two of those have contracts beyond this season.

It means the club need to figure out their long-term future there. And potentially name a successor to Virgil van Dijk .

Caught Offside claims Liverpool have a name in mind: Malick Thiaw. They're now monitoring the Newcastle United man as they weigh up a potential move next year.

Phase one ahead of a deal is underway, then. They'll start keeping tabs and, we imagine, have notified his agents that they're after more information.

Thiaw only joined Newcastle from AC Milan a year ago but he's become a proper regular for them. In fact, he's one of the more well-rounded centre-backs in the Premier League right now.

Naturally, that creates a problem as Thiaw wouldn't be cheap. He'd be very, very expensive, in fact, and we know Newcastle are completely against the idea of selling players to Liverpool right now.

But it's one to keep an eye out for. Liverpool will potentially need to replace Van Dijk, after all, and that will take an awful lot of money.

articles.title: Five stewards accused of assaulting Man United fan face stern punishment
articles.summary: 3 Five stewards have been severely punished after being accused of assaulting a Manchester United supporter last season.IncidentAccording to the Daily Mail,...
articles.body:
Five stewards have been severely punished after being accused of assaulting a Manchester United supporter last season.

According to the Daily Mail , the incident took place in April 2025 during the Manchester Derby.

United fans had staged a protest against the club's controversial decision to hike ticket prices. It's claimed that the five stewards attacked the man in the East Stand.

The individuals appeared at Manchester Magistrates' Court in January to face the music and now, it has been confirmed that they have been relieved of their duties.

It's understood that none of the five stewards was directly employed by United. All were contracted to Controlled Solutions Group, the club's appointed matchday security provider, and HR Security and Protection Services.

A CSG spokesperson told the Daily Mail, "The five staff that were supplied to CSG by HR Security and Protection Services are no longer allowed to work on any CSG operations."

Chris Wheeler and Nathan Salt note that this incident was discussed at length at the latest fans' forum at Old Trafford in July.

Fans highlighted "frustrations, anger and confusion with the communications between club and fans, with particular reference to the first wave of communications which were aggressive in tone, vague and anxiety provoking."

United were also challenged on the growing perception that the club is pricing out everyday supporters in pursuit of higher-yield hospitality and premium clientele.

Chief executive Omar Berrada replied, "There are no hidden intentions, the club is not trying to make financial gains from this process nor trying to reduce the number of season tickets available."

"We acknowledge there are learnings to be made from this investigation, and the initial communications should have been better to explain to fans what we are trying to do, and we will improve on this as a club. The relationship with our fans is fundamental and we want to protect them and the club."

United are next in action on Thursday when they face Sabah in their Champions League opener.

articles.title: Kennedy Crider leads Reagan volleyball over Brandeis to open District 27-6A
articles.summary: Crider notched 13 kills, and freshman Macy Glass added 12 to lead the potent Reagan attack as the Rattlers began their district title defense with a sweep of...
articles.body:
Led by hard-hitting Kennedy Crider and a solid front line, Reagan opened District 27-6A action by beating Brandeis in straight sets 25-22, 25-18, 25-11 Tuesday at Northside Sports Gym.

Crider, a senior outside hitter, led Reagan with 13 kills and added three aces as the Rattlers (19-10, 1-0) started their defense of the district crown on a positive note.

Freshman Macy Glass notched 12 kills and junior Reese Carver had seven to aid the Reagan attack.

The Rattlers fended off the Brandeis Broncos (18-12, 0-1) in a tight first set, 25-22, before taking the last two sets by comfortable margins.

"I think normally teams can get scared during the first set or they can settle after we do good after the first set, and we weren't satisfied for just one, we wanted all three (sets)," Crider said. "We wanted to show who we were. We came back up for what's on our chests, Reagan Rattlers, and like for each other. I think just not being satisfied with that one win and not being scared that it was close, we know what we have on our side of the court." Reagan coach Rachel Torvik said her squad prevailed over Brandeis because it stuck to the game plan.

"I think any district opening game is always just a true test of just focus and the fight that the kids have, and I think we finished really, really well tonight," Torvik said. "So, when we had a game plan, the kids listened to what we needed to do and they executed what I asked them to do, and I think we were pretty seamless tonight. I think there were moments of hiccups, but it wasn't because of a lack of effort on the kids' part."

Crider opened the match by serving the first two points for Reagan, including an ace, and proceeded to show her power at the net with four kills in the first set. The Rattlers were up 15-9 at one point before the Broncos, led by junior Allison Rodgers, went on a 12-5 run to tighten the match to get within 21-20 before Reagan closed out the set at 25-22, punctuated by two kills from Crider.

Reagan raced out to an 11-4 advantage in the second set and held the margin at five to six points the rest of the frame, before three consecutive kills from Mackenzie Chastain-Hunter, Carver and Crider closed out the set for the Rattlers at 25-17.

Sparked by an 11-2 run, Reagan again ran away from Brandeis in the final set as Carver and Crider each had five kills in the frame. Crider also notched another ace as the Rattlers cruised to close out the match, taking the set 25-11.

"(Crider) did a great job on the pin (outside), but I think that's also a tribute to just the balanced offense that we've been able to run this year," Torvik said. "Because both of our right sides (hitters) hit over .300 as well. Our middles are working hard in transition, and they may not get the ball a lot, but when they're up, they're effective and I think we're just doing a really good job of distributing the ball and keeping teams guessing as far as who's going to be receiving it."

Rodgers led Brandeis with 11 kills, followed by Rachel Markell with six, Olivia Munoz and Caliyah Lamkin with five apiece and Addison Wells with four.

Reagan continues district play against Churchill at 5:30 p.m. Friday at Blossom Athletic Center, while Brandeis has a week of rest before resuming its district slate with Churchill next Tuesday.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield’s Buccaneers Future Is Finally Settled After a Wild Offseason
articles.summary: Free agent? Not anymore. Baker Mayfield is here to stay in Tampa Bay. It’s pretty wild to think that just […]
articles.body:
Free agent? Not anymore. Baker Mayfield is here to stay in Tampa Bay . It's pretty wild to think that just three seasons ago, the Buccaneers handed Mayfield a one-year, $4 million prove-it-or-leave-it deal. Fast-forward to today, and the quarterback has gone from trying to earn his next contract to securing his long-term future on the Gulf Coast.

This offseason wasn't exactly a walk in the park, either. There was plenty of back-and-forth in the contract talks, with Mayfield even admitting that he felt disrespected during the process.

The timing made things even more interesting. Mayfield signed his previous deal in 2024, but with only three years on the contract, the Bucs knew they'd soon be back at the negotiating table with a big decision to make: extend their QB1 or let him test the waters again.

Baker Mayfield And Tampa Bay's Contract Standoff Finally Ends

What a difference a few weeks can make. Buccaneers training camp opened with Baker Mayfield publicly airing his frustration after contract talks stalled and Vita Vea reportedly wanting out. Fast-forward to Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, and somehow, both stars are sticking around Tampa Bay — and, more importantly, getting paid.

Mayfield has agreed to a three-year, $165 million extension with the Buccaneers, just hours before the Bucs kick off their season, keeping their QB1 in Tampa Bay for the foreseeable future. Adam Schefter broke the news on X .

And perhaps the most telling part? Tampa Bay never really wanted this to end any other way. The Buccaneers' GM told Athletic that they did not want to let Mayfield go.

The road to that extension, however, was anything but smooth.

Days later, the Bucs restructured Mayfield's contract, but the move added neither years nor new money. As the 2026 season approached, the lack of a long-term deal became an increasingly sore spot for the quarterback. Mayfield didn't exactly hide his frustration, and the contract standoff carried right into the doorstep of training camp.

Now, that drama is officially in the rearview mirror.

Since arriving in Tampa Bay, Mayfield has played with the swagger, creativity, and gunslinger mentality that made him a college football star at Oklahoma. He may never completely erase the questions that came with being the No. 1 overall pick, but the Bucs clearly believe they've seen enough.

Tampa Bay didn't just find a starting quarterback.

They found their quarterback — and now they're paying him like it.

articles.title: Torquay United beat nine-man Maidenhead 4-0
articles.summary: Torquay United claim their biggest victory in five months as they win 4-0 at nine-man Maidenhead United in National League South.
articles.body:
Torquay United got their biggest victory in five months as they won 4-0 at nine-man Maidenhead United in National League South.

The win - Torquay's third of the season - moves them up to eighth place in the table as they claimed back-to-back victories for the first time this season.

The Gulls could have scored more, having three goals disallowed as they produced a fine performance.

"I'm really pleased with the way we started," manager Jimmy Ball told BBC Radio Devon.

"I thought our first 15 minutes, we were really front-footed, we were really on top and we were really bright and sharp.

"That led to their right-sided centre-half getting booked, their left-sided centre-half getting booked and then ultimately if the left-sided boy doesn't make that tackle, we're on a counter-attack, so he had to make a rash tackle, and got himself sent off.

"We were on top so strongly they had to make those challenges, so we forced that - so the start I was really, really pleased with."

The hosts had Jordon Ragguette sent off after just 12 minutes for a reckless challenge on debutant Caleb Roberts .

It gave the Gulls the ascendency but Deon Moore had two goals ruled out for offside as the first half ended goalless.

Ragguette's defensive partner George Abbott was then sent off early in the second half for two yellow cards, and Ball's men finally broke the deadlock in the 54th minute when Cody Cooke converted from close range after Moore had headed back Angelo Cappello's cross.

Sonny-Blu Lo-Everton curled in an excellent second goal from the edge of the box four minutes later before Cooke had a goal ruled out for offside.

But the Gulls scored twice in the final seven minutes - Dan Hayfield made it 3-0 before Roberts' fellow Plymouth Argyle loanee, Tegan Finn, fired in low from the edge of the area for a debut goal.

It was an important win for Ball, who has been under pressure from sections of the Torquay support.

Last season's beaten play-off finalists have had a a stuttering start to the season, having won just one of their first six games before their recent resurgence.

"I just want to keep moving this team forward," added Ball. "There's been a lot of change, a lot of transition as a club, so it's not going to be smooth sailing

"I just need people to understand what I'm trying to do and and back what we're trying to do here because we are trying to change a few things to get a different result at the end of the season."

articles.title: 'Bottling it' - Garcia no-show for first Benn face-off
articles.summary: Conor Benn said Ryan Garcia "bottled" their first face-off after the American failed to turn up to their meeting on Tuesday in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia was a no-show for his first face-off with Conor Benn on Tuesday before their world title fight this weekend in Las Vegas.

The American was scheduled to attend a photo opportunity, but skipped it to leave Benn appearing alone.

Benn, 29, did have the company of his father, boxing legend Nigel Benn, who pretended to face off with his son.

After joking around with his dad, Benn said Garcia "didn't turn up".

"I apologise for Ryan doing what Ryan does and bottling it. We turn up, we're here, ready for the face-off," he said.

Garcia defends his WBC welterweight title at the T-Mobile Arena in Benn's first world championship bout.

The 28-year-old is the favourite for the contest and after failing to attend the first face-off of fight week, Garcia mocked Benn on Instagram.

"Nice relaxing time as Conor wastes time showing up to a face-off," he said.

"Back to the sauna you go, sausage getting cooked every way."

They are due to meet twice before fight night with the news conference on Thursday and the weigh-in on Friday.

Much has been made of Benn's weight cut for this contest, with the Briton having not fought at 10st 7lb (67kg) since 2022.

Benn had two fights with Chris Eubank Jr at middleweight before a 10st 12lb (69kg) catchweight against Regis Prograis in April.

Garcia has fought at lightweight and light-welterweight – missing weight for his light-welterweight contest against Devin Haney in 2024 – but is not expected to have issues with the weight, while Benn has said he does not intend to stay long at welterweight.

King tries to stop Mikaelian v Opetaia bout

In the co-main event on Saturday, Jai Opetaia is fighting Noel Mikaelian in a cruiserweight bout.

Mikaelian is the WBC champion, but could be stripped of the belt after withdrawing from his bout against the mandatory challenger in favour of facing the Australian.

Saturday's fight is further complicated by promoter Don King, who claims he has an exclusive deal with Mikaelian.

The veteran American promoter has sent a cease-and-desist letter to Zuffa Boxing and demanded the fight be cancelled.

Confirming Zuffa Boxing had received the legal letter, Dana White insisted the bout would be going ahead as planned.

"[Jai's] fighting this weekend," White said on Tuesday.

"I've always had good dealings with Don (King). When have you ever seen a scenario with us where we go and try to interfere with someone's contract?

articles.title: When it came out as Millwall, I have to admit I thought twice…
articles.summary: It’s funny how things sometimes fall for you. When it became apparent that I would be down south for work during this week, I decided that any away draw in o...
articles.body:
It's funny how things sometimes fall for you. When it became apparent that I would be down south for work during this week, I decided that any away draw in or near London would be a no-brainer.

With nine London clubs (plus Reading) in the hat, the odds were decent to say the least. When it came out as Millwall, I have to admit I thought twice, but in for a penny in for a pound.

I have no frame of reference for the Den. I was 13 last time we played away at Millwall at the old Den, so not only is it unlikely that I even know anyone to have ventured down, but even if I did it was a different ground back then.

Obviously, Millwall have a reputation, enhanced by various football dramas, as one of the roughest clubs in England.

I'm not going to pretend it's a total fabrication, but the days of firms meeting each other for pre-match scraps have been diluted a bit since the 80s and the relatively sedate nature of midweek cup ties meant this was no different to navigating any other unfamiliar neighbourhood on a random Tuesday night.

I did give them enough respect to travel entirely incognito and left my wife blissfully unaware that I'd be undertaking a solo venture to Bermondsey while away from home. Fair concessions I reckon.

You can become a bit spoilt when it comes to away travel if you're a fixture in the Premier League. The Den was a throwback to claustrophobic concourses, awful toilets and inadequate bars that were par for the course a couple of decades back. The staff did a canny job of distributing the Spitfire lager but they could have been better prepared for half-time (think of the SCR boost).

I headed into the stands with high expectations. I won't go into too much detail on this as you should all have been listening to The Mag podcast where I laid these out and will have recapped in the Millwall specific edition that will be dropping very soon, so use your ears for this part of the report.

Anyway, a strong United team lining up against an injury hit home side suggested this should be a formality. Instead the worry persisted that the shot-shy problems of last year are persisting into the Jaissle era. Constant possession produced nothing int he way of meaningful efforts as ponderous approach work invited the determined Millwall defence to thwart attacks before anyone dare do anything as outrageous as attempt a shot. Joe Willock finally had a go but home goalie Marschall produced a sharp save.

The breakthrough should arguably have come in the dying moments of the first half as Schar was clearly manhandled at a corner but nothing was given. Again, I'd urge you to tune into The Mag Pod to hear my foolish friend Simon Cahill insist that VAR is a bad thing.

Livramento stepped up his comeback with a half-time introduction but his presence did little to change things up, with Tino's rusty tracking at fault when Millwall almost nicked it, Arconte going on to crack the post. With the second half having deteriorated into fear of an old fashioned lower-league mugging, this was almost the killer moment. Instead, this moment was swiftly delivered at the right end almost instantly. Fernandez-Pardo had again looked lively off the bench, and his neatly disguised pass played in the clear man of the match, Lewis Hall . He drove it into the centre and Joe Willock cleverly diverted it inside the post, to cheers of outright relief behind the goal.

This, at least, was comfortable. Millwall were never likely to force penalties and the final whistle arrived to great cheers, despite the fact that no one can have been blown away by United's efforts on the night. Nonetheless, that maintains the unbeaten start to the season and the overall objective of any cup tie was achieved. We are in the hat for the next round.

A strange old week follows as we await the second tranche of the third round matches

before finding out the opponent in the crucial round of 16. Despite the misgivings over some performance elements this team continues to find a way and I made it out alive, so I'm chalking this one down as a massive success. Next.
