articles.title: Osaka makes passionate defence of on-court outfits
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her extravagant outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".

The 28-year-old is renowned for her eye-catching on-court attire, which included a hooded white gown for her first-round win against Anastasia Zakharova at the US Open.

Underneath was an all-black basketball-style kit in which Osaka played, while she also had her hair braided and wore a headband in a tribute to former NBA star Allen Iverson, who she called a "trailblazer" as "he's kind of like done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not".

In her latest outfit, Japan's four-time Grand Slam champion wore a decorated coat at the start of her last-16 US Open defeat by Elena Rybakina.

In defending her fashion statements, she referred to speaking out about her mental health in 2021 when she refused to speak to the media at the French Open and subsequently withdrew from the tournament.

Osaka, whose father is Haitian-American and mother is Japanese, also highlighted her ancestry.

"I don't mind being the first to do something and getting trashed for it," she wrote in a social media post.

"This happened when I talked about mental health and for some reason it's happening with my clothes lol.

"I'm literally Haitian it's in my blood to be this way, as long as the people after me have an easier path it's worth it."

articles.title: "Fabio is on fire!" – Dortmund star Silva earns praise after Villarreal cameo
articles.summary: Coming on with 15 minutes left of Borussia Dortmund's Champions League opener against Villarreal on Tuesday, Fabio Silva made a big impact in a short space o...
articles.body:
Coming on with 15 minutes left of Borussia Dortmund 's Champions League opener against Villarreal on Tuesday, Fabio Silva made a big impact in a short space of time to help his side to a 3-2 win.

Five minutes after coming on, the Portuguese forward raced in behind the Villarreal defence and set up striking partner Serhou Guirassy for the 2-1 goal. He also came close to scoring himself.

After the game, the 24-year-old received praise for his performance from both his teammates and head coach Niko Kovač.

"Fabio is on fire. He brings great energy to the game. He was lively today, ran a lot, and threatened from his first touch on the ball. It's fun playing with him. When he plays like this, he's very, very dangerous," said BVB goalkeeper Gregor Kobel on Prime.

Guirassy thanked Silva for the assist that led to the first of his two goals.

"I'm very happy with the result. It was a crazy game and once again a very special atmosphere. Of course, I'm very grateful to Fábio for his great assist," the Guinea international said.

Kovač is pleased to have the option of playing Guirassy and Silva together.

"You can see that we can play this system just as well as we can with one striker. We have flexibility and versatility," he said.

"Fabio is doing really well. He's blossoming, and that makes me happy.

"He works hard, creates lots of chances for the team. And, of course, he's someone who can provide assists. That's what we need."

articles.title: Wild scenes in City win! Security steps in, tunnel rocks
articles.summary: There was plenty of tension in that one! Emotions boiled over more than once between Manchester City and Porto last night.It all started in the first half wi...
articles.body:
There was plenty of tension in that one! Emotions boiled over more than once between Manchester City and Porto last night.

It all started in the first half with a foul by Marc Guéhi on Gabri Veiga . In an aerial challenge, the Man City star caught his opponent in the head with his arm, sending Veiga to the ground bleeding. The home side called for a sending-off, but the referee decided against showing either a yellow or a red card.

The players went into the break still fuming. According to English media reports, that led to a confrontation in the tunnel on the way to the dressing room. City goalkeeper Marcus Bettinelli was allegedly shoved by Porto officials. Ruben Dias is also said to have pushed head coach Francesco Farioli afterward. "Security staff from both teams had to intervene to separate players and staff from both sides as they entered the tunnel," Amazon Prime reporter Gabriel Clarke reported.

According to reports from inside the stadium, the tunnel could even be seen "shaking" during the clash between the teams, English outlet The Sun also reported.

When Enzo Maresca was asked about the tunnel scenes involving Dias after the match, the coach was clearly fed up: "How many times did you see me or my bench get up? Zero times in 95 minutes. How many times did you see their bench?..."

But that was not the last flashpoint of the evening. Shortly before full time, Erling Haaland and Pablo Rosario clashed on the pitch.

Haaland was wrestled to the ground by Rosario, and the two had to be separated by their teammates. Referee Szymon Marciniak showed both players a yellow card shortly afterward.

Adrian Durham, a reporter for English radio station talksport, sharply criticized Marciniak's handling of the situation. "Really naive from the referee," he said on air. "Rosario is basically just trying to get Haaland sent off, and that's a disgrace. A really weak refereeing performance."

Haaland himself did not comment on the scuffle after the final whistle, but he was realistic when speaking to the club's own media: "We knew it was going to be a hard battle. Under that huge pressure, we had to deliver on the biggest stage, and we did that today."

The striker had plenty of reason to celebrate anyway: along with being named Man of the Match and scoring both goals in the 2-0 win, he also matched a club legend. The Norwegian has now scored as many Champions League goals for Manchester City as Sergio Aguero (36). That means he needs just one more to move past the Argentine.

In the all-time Champions League scoring charts, Haaland also moved ahead of Thomas Müller and now sits seventh with 59 goals in total. Particularly remarkable is his average of exactly one goal per game. For comparison, Lionel Messi needed 80 appearances in the competition to reach 60 goals.

articles.title: Belgium battle could be a blessing
articles.summary: It is a new chapter for Aston Villa and, against Club Brugge, they turned the page.  A first win of the season, albeit more nervy than anticipated, lit the s...
articles.body:
It is a new chapter for Aston Villa and, against Club Brugge, they turned the page.

A first win of the season, albeit more nervy than anticipated, lit the spark for Unai Emery's side.

The visitors were in a commanding and deserved position at half-time, John McGinn 's opener making him the club's all-time record European goalscorer with 12.

Emi Buendia 's strike and Nicolas Jackson 's first Villa goal - benefiting from Yann Sommer 's rush of blood - had them cruising.

Brugge were poor and George Hemmings , Villa's first Champions League/European Cup teenage starter in 43 years, could have had at least one.

Yet the hosts made it uncomfortable for Unai Emery's men with Nicolo Tresoldi 's penalty after Aaron Wan-Bissaka 's blatant handball setting up an anxious last half an hour, during which Tresoldi hit the post.

It can be viewed as a blessing in disguise that Villa had to battle their way through and ride out the hosts' pressure to earn their first win of the season - adding the grit and determination to the quality of the opening half to prove they can get the job done.

Not that they needed the evidence themselves, Emery and his squad always have that faith and the internal desire to progress no matter the obstacle.

It was the same last season. A below-par 1-0 win over limited Bologna - thanks to another McGinn goal - got Villa going and they hardly looked back.

The victory kicked off the staggering run of 17 wins in 20 games which formed the backbone of returning to the Champions League and giving Villa momentum to win the Europa League.

Since then, of course, Villa's spine has been torn out and Emery has to integrate 10 new players into his methodical methods.

Three points in Brugge may not spark another relentless run but it gives Emery and Villa the foundations of this new era.

articles.title: Ben Shelton shocks Carlos Alcaraz in five sets to win US Open quarterfinal
articles.summary: Shelton comes through in a 6-7 (5-7), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-6) epic against defending champion Alcaraz.
articles.body:
Ben Shelton has stamped his authority on his home tennis Grand Slam by overcoming two-time champion Carlos Alcaraz in an all-time classic US Open quarterfinal that lasted four hours and 28 minutes at the Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York.

Shelton held his nerve in the final set tie-break to win the nail-biting match with a 6-7 (5-7), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-6) scoreline in the latest finish to a US Open match on Wednesday morning.

The American, seeded eighth in the tournament, enjoyed the home support despite the popularity of the Spaniard, who was looking to defend his title after an injury-enforced layoff.

Shelton will face compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the last four, setting up the prospect of an American finalist for the first time since 2003.

Following the win, Shelton credited the crowd’s support for helping him pull through the thrilling contest.

“Whether it’s my coaches and my team there, all my family and friends here, or the city of New York that showed up tonight till 3am with the USA chants until the very end,” the smiling semifinalist said.

“That’s what kept me going, and that’s what got me this win tonight.

“It’s incredible. I always say that this is the greatest sports city in the world. I say that this is the greatest stadium in the world.”

Alcaraz, seeded third upon his comeback after four months, started brightly by winning the first set before Shelton pushed the seven-time Grand Slam winner into a string of unforced errors.

Shelton, the highest-seeded American men’s singles player in the final Grand Slam of the year, gave the raucous crowd much to cheer for as he raced to win the second and third sets.

In a battle of two 23-year-old talents, Alcaraz came back to win the fourth set and take the match to the deciding fifth set but struggled to sustain his comeback.

The defending champion struggled at several moments in the final set and appeared to have vomited into his towel during a break.

However, Alcaraz pushed the home favourite until the end but fell short when the fifth set was forced into a tie-break. He showed flashes of his usual tenacity and comeback spirit, but it was not enough to see Alcaraz over the line this time.

At the end of the four-and-a-half-hour epic, both players shared smiles, words of encouragement and a long embrace at the net.

“To be here in front of you guys tonight is an absolute honour,” Shelton said in his on-court interview. “Sharing the court with Carlos is an absolute honour, and I cherish every moment I have out here.”

“That was a war, epic match, so physical,” Shelton said. “Carlos is one of the greatest champions in our sport already, at 23 years old.

“It’s always fun being on the court against him. It’s ridiculous some of the stuff he comes up with sometimes – the most enjoyable match that I’ve had in my career, for sure.”

articles.title: De Londres 2012 a Vietnam 2026: "Cuando tenga 80 años seguiré haciendo deporte porque ayuda a ser feliz"
articles.standfirst: Zuriñe Rodríguez fue triatleta olímpica y hoy 14 años después dirige al equipo de Seniors del Desafío Santalucia
articles.summary: Zuriñe Rodríguez fue triatleta olímpica y hoy 14 años después dirige al equipo de Seniors del Desafío Santalucia
articles.body: De triatleta olímpica en Londres 2012 a directora de orquesta en el Desafío Santalucia Vietnam 2026. Zuriñe Rodríguez es una apasionada del deporte y estos días está viviendo una experiencia única dirigiendo al quinteto de expedicionarios seniors formado por Pilar, José, Pablo, Enrique y Rafa. "Está siendo una aventura increíble. A mí siempre me gustó la bici, pero he descubierto junto a este gran equipo cómo disfrutar de grandes momentos rapelando, haciendo una vía ferrata o los trekking durísimos en la selva", afirma Zuriñe. Aquella chica de Barakaldo que había convertido el triatlón en su vida y que en Londres 2012 se enfrentó a los 1.500 metros de natación, 40 kilómetros de bicicleta y 10 corriendo de la prueba olímpica hoy disfruta 14 años después liderando en Vietnam el equipo de Seniors entre 68 y 79 años que estos días viven su gran aventura deportiva gracias al Desafío Santalucia, un proyecto que aborda la longevidad activa con el deporte como gran herramienta. "Mi vida no se entiende sin deporte, aunque es verdad que acabé saturada tras 13 años en la élite. Entrenaba a la semana más de las 35 horas semanales que hoy trabajo. Y lo dejé porque mi cabeza quería seguir mientras mi cuerpo decía basta. Pero me entró el gusanillo con un amigo, nos apuntamos a la Titan Desert y ganamos en dúo mixto. Y eso me hizo plantearme en 2016 volver a intentar llegar a los Juegos de Tokio", recuerda Zuriñe sobre su carrera deportiva. "Me siento aventurera y estoy convencida que a los 80 años seguiré haciendo cualquier deporte como estos expedicionarios del Desafío. Cada vez hay más gente mayor en los gimnasios, en las montañas, montando en bici... El deporte ayuda a ser feliz", afirma Zuriñe. La directora deportiva del Desafío Santalucia lanza este mensaje a los mayores: "Nunca es tarde para empezar. La mente es importante y hay que trabajarla. A Rafa, Pilar, José, Pablo y Quique les digo que todo cuenta: movilidad, fuerza, descanso, buena nutrición, confianza, creer en ti...". Enrique González forma parte de la expedición en Vietnam y ha sido el encargado de diseñar las rutas por Vietnam: "Un año antes empezamos a hacer el scouting una vez decidido el país... En Vietnam hay dos partes del Desafío, uno enfocado en la bici que entre conductores y guías hizo que necesitáramos 12 personas y otro más complejo en la zona de las cuevas que entre guías, porteadores, cocineros, el doctor... pues entre 45 y 50 personas". "Llevo trabajando en el Reto Pelayo Vida y el Desafío Santalucia desde que conocí a Eric Frattini en 2017. Soy propietario de la empresa TarannaTrekking y empecé años atrás con Jesús Calleja con la producción audiovisual de aventura. Y luego con Trex he trabajado en todos los destinos menos los de barco", afirma Enrique, más conocido en la expedición como Taranná por el nombre de su empresa. A la hora de elegir un destino de todos los que ha diseñado, Enrique cree que "el de Vietnam en términos visuales puede ser el más redondo junto al de Costa Rica, pero me cuesta elegir uno porque también recuerdo mucho el primero en Nepal con el Annapurna".

articles.title: El deporte de Ceuta pide auxilio: "Nos hemos sentido abandonados, traicionados y humillados"
articles.standfirst: El deporte ceutí pide ayuda ante una situación "límite e insostenible".
articles.summary: El deporte ceutí pide ayuda ante una situación "límite e insostenible".
articles.body: El salto masivo que se produjo en Ceuta el pasado 30 de julio ha sido un golpe demoledor para la ciudad. Las consecuencias van más allá de una evidente crisis migratoria y los vecinos empiezan a acusar las semanas ineficiencia política. La crisis ya es también social, psicológica, sanitaria, de seguridad y, por supuesto, deportiva. Los profesionales, aficionados y niños de la ciudad no pueden practicar sus deportes con normalidad. Algunas instalaciones todavía no están disponibles, otras no son seguras y en lugares como la Bahía Sur, que acoge la mayoría de deportes acuáticos, “no se pueden garantizar las condiciones de higiene”. Bastan unos días en la ciudad autónoma para darse cuenta de la dimensión de un problema que ha afectado directamente a uno de los motores económicos y sociales de la ciudad: el deporte. Antes del 30 de julio, el Monte Hacho era un escenario habitual de rutas en bicicleta o caminatas. Su ladera está llena de senderos que los ceutíes recorren para mimetizarse con la naturaleza y disfrutar del deporte y el aire puro. Uno de ellos es Ángel González, que aprovecha su cuenta de instagram (@ceutaenbici) para promocionar rutas por el entorno de la ciudad: “Esta zona estaba bastante repleta de estos señores. Montaron aquí sus asentamientos y los caminos están con piedras, ramas y muchísima basura por donde han pasado. Lo han dejado todo dando pena. Ahora hay que ir con mil ojos porque está lleno de obstáculos que no había antes. De troncos y piedras que han utilizado para sus campamentos improvisados. Hasta hace unos días esto estaba completo. Y podías encontrarte algún inmigrante que te saltara a la pista o escondidos por cualquier lado”, explica. Una situación que pone en jaque la seguridad de los caballas. “La gente tiene miedo a salir sola a hacer deporte. Se han creado grupos de WhatsApp para incentivar y ayudar un poco el poder salir”, asegura Ángel. Pero el problema no está sólo en el monte o la periferia de la ciudad. El Bulldogs Hockey Club tampoco ha podido retomar la actividad de su escuela, donde entrenan 70 jóvenes, en su mayoría niñas. “Traer a esta pista al aire libre a niñas de 11 a 19 años... Ellas vienen con la ropa más ceñida para hacer deporte y ya hemos tenido problemas con gente que venía y sacaba los móviles. A mí me ha habido madres que me han notificado que sus hijas no vienen porque tienen miedo. Y es razonable porque no saben quién ha entrado, no saben lo que ha hecho. Ya ha habido violaciones. Tú no sabes lo que le pueden hacer a tu niña a las 9 de la noche, que es cuando nosotros acabamos la escuela de hockey”, explica José Antonio Vera, presidente del club. La situación no varía si se trata de deportes acuáticos. El comodoro del Club Náutico de Ceuta, Milenko González, lamenta que todas sus actividades “se realizan en un medio abierto, que es el mar por el que han llegado los inmigrantes. Todo se junta en nuestro medio: inseguridad, muertes, insalubridad... Aquí la promoción del deporte ha llevado muchísimo esfuerzo. Es mucho trabajo como para, que de la noche a la mañana, desaparezca todo y tengamos que partir de cero”, asegura. Las imágenes que se acumulan en la retira de la población de Ceuta son desoladoras y, algunas de ellas, difíciles de olvidar por su brutalidad y dureza. Así lo explica José Ismael Rodríguez, el presidente de la Federación de Aguas Abiertas de Ceuta: “Nuestros nadadores se han encontrado cadáveres en el mar. Yo el día 30 estaba en la frontera y también tuve la mala suerte de ver cadáveres porque estaba allí desplazado. E impresiona mucho. Los nadadores entran en pánico. Nos hemos encontrado a gente incluso ahogándose. Y eso es más fácil, simplemente tienes que ayudarlos a llegar a la orilla, pero con un cadáver... Nuestros fondos marinos son un desastre ecológico. Todo va al mar. El día de la entrada era un río de ropa, chanclas, flotadores... Ahora mismo el fondo marino de Ceuta es un desastre”. Y nadie conoce mejor el fondo marino de la ciudad que Eusebio Álvarez, el Presidente de la Federación de Actividades Subacuáticas de Ceuta: “Hemos hecho batidas para limpiar todos esos residuos que son contaminantes. Íbamos a organizar actividades de buceo con niños en la Bahía Sur durante el mes de agosto, pero hemos tenido que cancelarlas. No podíamos garantizar la higiene ni la seguridad de los niños. No queremos que ningún niño se encuentre a alguien ahogado, ya que puede ser un shock bastante importante”, confiesa. Para Ignacio Tendero, presidente de la Federación de Vela de Ceuta, el foco también está en la Bahía Sur. “Es una zona más protegida y donde se realizan los deportes náuticos. Si eres padre y te enteras de que hay un brote de sarna, o simplemente ves las imágenes en la televisión... Ceuta es muy pequeño, en diez minutos están en la playa y ves el tipo de gente que hay, cómo están montando cabañas... Pues con esas condiciones sanitarias y de seguridad no se puede hacer nada”. La situación ha obligado a cancelar numerosos torneos. En pádel, por ejemplo, han tenido que renunciar a su campeonato internacional. “El mismo día del asalto empezamos a valorarlo. En el centro hay cierta seguridad, pero el resto de la ciudad está muy comprometida. Hay un colapso total de los servicios. Normalmente no hay que usarlos, pero en un torneo de este nivel tienes que saber que están disponibles. No debemos tensionarlo más con la organización de un evento, por eso lo suspendimos. Eso sí, el año que viene intentaremos que sea la mejor edición de la historia”, desvela Agustín Atencia, Presidente de la Federación de Pádel. Para ‘Tini’, como se le conoce en la ciudad, “la población de Ceuta es la gran perjudicada". Un sentimiento que comparte el Director General de Deportes de Ceuta, Sergio Aguilera: “Nos hemos sentido abandonados, traicionados y humillados. Y así nos seguimos sintiendo porque todavía no hay un plan. Necesitamos recuperar la normalidad, recuperar nuestra vida. Llevamos desde el principio de la legislatura apostando muy fuerte por potenciar el turismo de la ciudad a través de la organización de eventos deportivos y esto ha sido un palo importante para esa estrategia. El mensaje de Aguilera es claro: “Animamos a la gente a que siga participando en nuestras pruebas. Y a los que no han venido, les digo que, si tienen la oportunidad, que lo hagan. Es el momento para conocer Ceuta, para que puedan ver lo que está pasando. Ceuta es España, lo es por los cuatro costados, y estamos orgullosos de pertenecer a esta gran nación”, sentencia.

articles.title: The absurd battle between the SEC and LSU reaches a tipping point
articles.summary: LSU is being a thorn in the side of its SEC siblings in a preposterous battle of egos that has sucked the oxygen out of college football.
articles.body: Lane Kiffin couldn’t help himself. At halftime, as his LSU team took a 31-3 lead over Clemson into the locker room, the Tigers’ head coach was about to dash off after chatting with ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe. And then he leaned back in. “Imagine if we had pro players,” he quipped. That’s line-item number 90 in the Southeastern Conference’s amended complaint, filed on Tuesday in a federal courtroom. The league, clearly fed up and disgusted with Lane being Lane, has asked the Northern District Court of Alabama for a temporary restraining order to ensure that no one from LSU can block or interfere with, among other things, a meeting scheduled for Thursday to discuss whether the conference ought to boot the school from its membership. “The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed,” the league said in a statement. “A commitment to those rules, and to the core principles of the Southeastern Conference, is an essential element of SEC membership. Today’s filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference’s ability to govern competition among its members.” It likely won’t come to that. This feels like posturing from a rightfully exasperated Greg Sankey and his other 15 university presidents. The thought of the SEC expelling one of its charter members after 94 years of inclusion seems preposterous. Of course, LSU – which stomped Clemson 51-10 on Saturday – dying on a hill over two guys who couldn’t even make it in the NFL, also is ridiculous. Besides LSU, despite its blustering and blathering, already blinked first. On the eve of the Tigers’ game against Clemson on Friday, Kiffin opted not to add Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to the roster, arguing that without knowing the full ramifications of their inclusion, it was in the best interest of the football program to sit them out. Except, LSU couldn’t stop there. The school also said it would leave two roster spots open, just in case they change their mind later. That, coupled with Kiffin’s smart-aleck quip to Rowe is why we’re here, with a scheduled Zoom meeting on Thursday to discuss expulsion. It appears the Tigers may be blinking again after the SEC’s filing on Tuesday. Multiple reports on Tuesday night indicated the two open roster spots were filled by players other than Wright and Harris, meaning they will not play for LSU this season. The whole thing, frankly, feels a lot like when my kids were little. My son was great at needling my daughter in ways he knew would get a rise out of her, and my daughter could never not take the bait. Parenting wound up being a lot of “you stop annoying your sister and you stop falling for it.” So, Lane. Please stop annoying Greg. And Greg, for the love of God, stop falling for it. And everyone stop whining to their mom about the other one – or in this case, a federal judge. LSU has clearly decided to not only live in the swill of the college athletics pigsty, but to flop about in it. Goaded on by a governor, who handpicked the university president and staged a coup to overthrow one athletic director in order to hire Kiffin, the bayou bandits are proudly wearing their black hats. In a video alleged to be from the Tigers’ locker room at the half against Clemson, someone screams, “The whole world f**king hates you. Let’s go tell the whole world to f**k off.’’ Meanwhile, basketball coach Will Wade currently has a roster of only four players a month before official practice begins. By rule, you need five, though perhaps one could sue for an exception? Anyway, that’s because Wade – who got fired from the school after an NCAA investigation four years ago only to return in black-hatted triumph – is trying to bring RJ Luis, who signed an NBA contract, and a host of guys involved in fifth-year eligibility court orders to campus. So yes, LSU is off the rails. They are spending who-knows-how-much in billable hours to add two players they really don’t need to the roster. It is not about principle, as that requires those involved to actually possess them. It is about thumbing their nose at authority and being a thorn in the side of its SEC siblings. It’s about being right about being wrong. It is a preposterous battle of egos that has sucked the oxygen out of college football. If they haven’t yet, Michigan, Big Ten clock officials, Rutgers and the Florida State facilities team ought to each send Kiffin a big ol’ bouquet. The SEC is not only within its rights to try to find a way to penalize one of its members for bad behavior; it has been left with no other real choice. That a Louisiana judge handcuffed the conference with a ruling that says it couldn’t penalize LSU for breaking one of its rules is jurisprudence of the absurd. Sankey is wise to seek relief from more absurdity. Back when my kids got to instigating and overreacting, I’d try to rationalize with them. Tell them that they were meant to be each other’s champions, and that one day they’d only have each other. Except kids being kids, my son would keep needling and my daughter would keep wailing. Eventually, I’d reach the tipping point that every parent eventually reaches: Knock it off. Or else. Here’s hoping this is the SEC’s tipping point. Or else.

articles.title: Predicting WWE's 10 Top Stars in 2030
articles.summary: WWE has been a mainstay in pro wrestling and American entertainment for decades, and that does not appear to be changing anytime soon.
articles.body:
WWE has been a mainstay in pro wrestling and American entertainment for decades, and that does not appear to be changing anytime soon.

While the company might be at a stagnant point right now, it is also more mainstream than ever.

The partnership with Netflix has increased Raw's reach, and its partnership with ESPN has made it more affordable for many fans to enjoy PLEs.

However, the bread and butter will always be the men and women of WWE. Without them, there is no product.

The company has a great crop of talent right now that is poised to lead it into the next decade. Let's look at some of the stars who could be runnin WWE by 2030.

Trick Williams might be the easiest slam dunk decision when it comes to choosing the next crop of main event talent.

Even if you take away Lil Yachty as his manager and the fur and the special entrance, Williams would still stand out as a special talent because those trappings are not what make him good.

Trick Willy is like the perfect recipe for a WWE Superstar. He's in great shape, he's tall, he has enviable mic skills, and he can have a fun match with just about anyone.

His feud with Carmelo Hayes may have put him on the map, but Williams is still here because he is too good to keep down.

WWE has needed a youth movement for quite some time, and the man who could lead that movement is Je'Von Evans.

The Young OG has been nothing short of phenomenal, both in NXT and on the main roster. His high-flying style makes his matches must-see TV, but it's his personality the fans connect with the most.

Evans is not playing some boisterous character he made up. He's just being himself, and that is what makes him so likeable.

It's tough to say when he might be ready for a world title run, but it wouldn't be surprising to see him start earning title shots in 2027.

Watching the rise of Chelsea Green from her start on Tough Enough, her time in TNA, and now being the WWE champion has been amazing to watch.

Few people embody a hardworking attitude more than she does. She has taken every single idea WWE has given her, some of which were terrible, and made them work.

The crowd has grown to love her, not just for her hilarious antics, but for her clear and genuine love for this business.

Green is someone who could be important to WWE for years to come if she is booked properly.

WWE has been hyping the main roster debut of Lola Vice through video packages in recent weeks after she had a successful run in NXT.

On paper, Vice has everything WWE could want. She has legit fighting skills from her MMA background, she has charisma to spare, and she has a very marketable look.

She is still growing as a performer, so we will likely continue to see her get better as she works her way through the main roster.

Vice has also been an important part of WWE's work with AAA, and that is probably going to continue for the foreseeable future.

We may not like having to include him on the list, but there is no denying how important Dominik Mysterio has become in WWE.

He has officially stepped out of his father's shadow and become his own man over the past couple of years, and it's the best thing that could have happened to him.

His runs with the IC and AAA Mega Championships have given him a nice boost in exposure, and his stable has helped keep him relevant.

Dirty Dom has mastered the art of being a dirtbag, and if he continues on this path, he could be a top heel by the end of next year.

When he first arrived on the scene, Solo Sikoa was portrayed as more of a silent killer type, but he has grown into one of the most entertaining guys on the main roster.

His brand of wit and sarcasm always makes his promos fun, and his physical dominance makes it easy to back up what he says.

Allowing him to show off his lighter side while teaming with LA Knight has been a joy to watch, and it doesn't appear to be slowing down.

The never-ending Bloodline story has pulled him back in, but if he is ever able to break free from it, he is going to be much better off.

The Judgment Day has had a lot of ups and downs over the last year, and unfortunately for her, Roxanne Perez often feels like the odd woman out.

Liv Morgan has her world title, Raquel Rodriguez has the Intercontinental Championship, and the boys have their own issues to worry about.

Once Roxy is able to distance herself from the group and return to her babyface roots, she is going to take off in popularity.

Fans in NXT know, but fans who only watch the main roster have no idea how good of an underdog she is, but they will find out soon.

While Sol Ruca's booking may not always be the most consistent, there are clear signs that management sees her as a potential main event star.

Ruca has her own unique style that helps her stand out from the rest of the roster, but it's her agility and exciting offense that get people cheering.

The Sol Snatcher has become one of those moves that fans look forward to seeing every time she wrestles because it's just that cool.

Being the son of a Steiner may have helped him get his foot in the door, but Bron Breakker's skill is what will carry him to the top of the mountain.

Few people have the kind of raw athleticism and intensity that Breakker possesses, and it makes him a unique talent in an industry full of people who feel like carbon copies of each other.

Being with The Vision has helped keep him relevant, but it wouldn't be surprising to see Breakker step away from the group in 2027 to focus on himself.

It's not a matter of if he will win a world title, it's a matter of when.

If it's not obvious to you that Oba Femi has been marked as a future top star in WWE, then you haven't been paying attention.

Winning the King of the Ring was definitely a nice feather in his cap, but beating Brock Lesnar twice in the same calendar year is his greatest accomplishment to date.

WWE even hyped him and Breakker as the future of WWE leading up to their Sunday Night's Main Event match.

Femi has the aura, the physical ability and the drive to be successful, and if WWE continues to book him as strongly as it has, he is going to have a great 2027.

articles.title: 10 of the Most Wildly Expensive Athlete Cars
articles.summary: Star athletes tend to have many millions in disposable income. They often use that money to purchase flashy cars.
articles.body:
Star athletes tend to have many millions in disposable income. They often use that money to purchase flashy cars.

For some, these vehicles are incredibly expensive.

LeBron James, Erling Haaland and Cristiano Ronaldo are just three examples of world-famous athletes who have flexed their financial muscle on the road. They've all built up a spectacular collection of vehicles.

Here, we've assembled some of the most expensive athlete cars.

Due to the challenges of proving ownership, not all rumors are included. For example, big-name athletes such as Lionel Messi, Tom Brady and Aaron Judge are connected with million-dollar machines, but the reports are unconfirmed.

As a result, the list—carefully researched but potentially volatile—isn't comprehensive. Nevertheless, it sure is impressive.

It's only fitting that a world-famous wheelman has a spectacular car, right?

Fernando Alonso, a two-time Formula 1 champion and Aston Martin driver, recently purchased a "unicorn" Pagani Zonda Diamante Verde. He was spotted with the gorgeous V12 in Monaco.

While the price is unconfirmed, Carscoops noted that one-off Zonda 760 series models are trading for more than $10 million.

Among the athletes with these wildly expensive cars, there are many superstars from the soccer—yes, fútbol—world.

Karim Benzema, who rose to prominence as a striker for Real Madrid, is the first such example. A few years ago, he went through his garage and showed off a dazzling Bugatti Chiron in addition to several other pricey vehicles.

Most reports place the value of the Chiron hypercar north of $3 million.

Along his ascent from RB Salzburg to Borussia Dortmund to Manchester City, Erling Haaland has accumulated a sparkling fleet.

Your favorite may be a Ferrari Monza SP2 or Ferrari 812 Superfast. You might prefer his Mercedes-AMG One or even appreciate his Rolls-Royce Cullinan. The list in Haaling's possession is as extraordinary as it is extensive.

But the spotlight is gleaming on the Bugatti Tourbillon, a $5 million hypercar that he reportedly bought with Norwegian billionaire Ole Ertvaag.

The second Formula 1 icon in the fold, Lewis Hamilton's priciest ride, is a proper match for his professional ties.

Hamilton, a driver for Ferrari, showed up to Monza in a coveted F40.

The story behind his purchase is spectacular as well.

In an Instagram post , Hamilton said the F40 sat in a garage for 30 years. "Master engineers and mechanics at the factory worked for weeks to bring her back to life," he said.

According to ESPN's Laurence Edmondson , the supercar has surpassed $8 million at auction at its highest value.

Among the best scorers of his generation, former striker Zlatan Ibrahimovic is known for an uncommon level of self-confidence.

"I am like a Ferrari among Fiats," he said in 2019 .

On its own, that quote is fantastic. It's even better knowing he purchased a Ferrari Monza SP2—worth approximately $2 million—around that time.

Also, for several years, Ibrahimovic has posted an image of an expensive car with the caption "Happy Birthday to Zlatan." In 2025 , that was a Ferrari F80 valued at $4.4 million. That'd be a heck of a birthday present.

The greatest player of his generation—at the very least—LeBron James has enjoyed a well-traveled career with four different NBA franchises.

When he's on the road, The King is moving in style, too.

LeBron's fascination with vehicles can be attributed to his childhood. "I was always inspired to have great cars and drive great cars," he told Vanity Fair . "That's just the little-inner-city-kid aspiration."

In a garage boasting Ferraris, a Lamborghini and more, James' reported prize is a Porsche 918 Spyder. The estimated value is north of $1.4 million.

In perhaps the most natural NBA transition possible, we shift from LeBron James to none other than Michael Jordan.

Back in 2024, Automobili Pininfarina shared a picture of the basketball legend taking delivery of a one-off Battista Targamerica. It's a specially built open-top variant that includes a cigar holder and humidor.

Due to the hypercar's customization—plus its ownership connection—its value is dynamic. It's likely above the typical $2-plus million for a Battista.

Jordan, who co-owns a NASCAR team, clearly has a love for the road.

Behind many years of stardom at European giants Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, Neymar is a world-famous playmaker on the pitch.

And the Brazilian's car collection isn't so bad, either.

Neymar added a $1.25 million Ferrari Purosangue SUV to his garage in 2025. That may be the jewel, although there are unconfirmed reports of a rare Lamborghini Veneno—one with an estimated value of $4.5 million.

Oh, and he has a replica Batmobile . Pretty sweet.

The options at Cristiano Ronaldo's disposal are nothing short of incredible.

Ronaldo, one of the greatest scorers in fútbol history, has used a portion of his immense wealth to amass a deep collection of vehicles. He showed off that impressive garage in an Instagram post .

Among the many high-dollar cars, the headliner is a white Bugatti Centodieci—an incredibly rare build that carries a $10 million price tag.

The total value of Ronaldo's fleet must be astounding.

Shortly before Max Verstappen ripped off four straight F1 titles, he had a chance to test the Aston Martin Valkyrie while in the prototype stage.

"It was a lot of fun out there," he said .

That's surely a vast understatement of the Valkyrie, which Verstappen now owns. He was seen driving the $3.5 million machine in a 2023 video.

Given his status as one of the most accomplished F1 drivers ever, Verstappen is quite literally the perfect person for such a stunning hypercar.

articles.title: Dura crítica a los continuos cambios de pareja: “No somos un deporte serio”
articles.standfirst: Gonzalo Rubio reflexiona sobre la falta de continuidad en los proyectos de Premier Padel y aboga por una regulación de cara a 2027
articles.summary: Gonzalo Rubio reflexiona sobre la falta de continuidad en los proyectos de Premier Padel y aboga por una regulación de cara a 2027
articles.body: Los cambios de pareja son una constante en el pádel profesional y una dinámica frecuente en el circuito actual. La duración de los proyectos tiende a ser más reducida y son habituales las permutaciones de compañeros a lo largo de un mismo curso. Sobre este contexto se ha pronunciado Gonzalo Rubio, uno de los jugadores más experimentados de Premier Padel, quien ha compartido su visión a través de sus redes sociales tras finalizar su participación en el Paris Major. El sevillano competía junto a Álvaro Montiel, dupla que no tendrá continuidad en las próximas citas, tal y como el propio jugador ha confirmado en una publicación en Instagram: “Mi compañero decidió, después de dos torneos, jugar el siguiente con otro jugador. Es una decisión totalmente lícita, y no va de él: va del marco que lo permite. Hoy el reglamento lo permite todo. Cada vez los ‘proyectos’ —por llamarlos de alguna manera— duran menos. Torneo sí, torneo también, cambio de pareja”. Actualmente, la normativa del circuito no fija un límite de modificaciones de pareja por temporada. Se trata de un debate recurrente en el sector, respecto al cual la Federación Internacional de Pádel (FIP) ha manifestado en diversas ocasiones estar estudiando posibles vías de regulación, considerando los condicionantes técnicos y las situaciones derivadas de lesiones de los deportistas. En su análisis, Rubio aborda la evolución que, a su juicio, ha tenido el impacto mediático y deportivo de estas variaciones: “Durante años se justificó con que los cambios eran el salseo, lo que vendía desde los medios. Sinceramente, creo que hemos llegado a un punto en el que ya ni eso: de tantos cambios, la noticia ha dejado de ser noticia”. Y añade: “Seamos honestos: todavía no somos un deporte serio”. Asimismo, el jugador andaluz expone el impacto que esta dinámicas genera en los distintos estamentos del pádel: “El aficionado que paga una entrada o que trata de seguir el circuito profesional merece identificarse con parejas que se consoliden y ganen una identidad con el tiempo. Los entrenadores merecen poder planificar. Los jugadores merecemos trabajar con un horizonte coherente y digno. Los patrocinadores merecen saber a qué proyecto se suben. Creo y espero que junto a la FIP se pueda construir un reglamento sólido que regule con coherencia el límite de cambios de compañero por temporada, de cara a 2027. No para prohibir: para ordenar”. Para concluir, Rubio puntualiza que su planteamiento responde a una propuesta constructiva en beneficio del crecimiento de la disciplina: “La hago desde dentro, como jugador, con el único objetivo de que entre todos construyamos un deporte más serio y mejor regulado. Ojalá algún día dejemos de repetir que el pádel es un deporte individual que se juega en parejas. Que podamos decir que aquí no gana el mejor jugador, gana la mejor pareja”.

articles.title: Lionel Messi agrees deal to buy second-tier Spanish club Eldense
articles.summary: Messi poised to become majority owner of a second club in Spain after the purchase of fifth-tier UE Cornella in April.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has reached an agreement in principle to become the new owner of Spanish second-division side CD Eldense, the club has confirmed.

“At this time, the operation is pending completion of the final legal and contractual procedures, including the corresponding due diligence process, as well as the mandatory authorisation from the High Council for Sports (CSD),” Eldense told the Reuters news agency.

The Inter Miami forward is close to completing a deal to purchase 100 percent of the shares held by Colombian investment group TH Soluciones Group SAS, the current majority shareholder.

Messi, 39, is poised to become the majority owner of a second club in Spain after the purchase of UE Cornella in Spain’s fifth tier on April 16 earlier this year.

He is also set to receive a stake in his current club Inter Miami after the expiry of his playing contract. Reports in Spain on Tuesday said the deal to purchase Eldense is expected to be completed in the coming days.

The club were unable to give a fixed date for the completion of the deal.

Eldense, 20th in the Segunda standings, were taken over by TH Soluciones Group last October. Eldense have risen to the second tier of Spanish football after years spent in the regional divisions.

articles.title: The Rise, Fall, And Rise Again of WWE's The Vision
articles.summary: No act has had a more tumultuous last 16 months in WWE than The Vision.
articles.body:
No act has had a more tumultuous last 16 months in WWE than The Vision.

Arriving on the scene as a faction of young stars surrounding Seth Rollins, with the hope that his star power would elevate them to the top of the card, the group quickly became the centerpiece of the Raw brand's main event scene.

Then injuries struck, with Rollins going down with a torn rotator cuff in October 2025, new de facto leader Bron Breakker suffering a severe hernia, and Bronson Reed tearing his triceps, leaving Austin Theory and Logan Paul as the only active members of the group.

Along the line, significant creative plans for all were affected, as seen on WWE Unreal , which documented Breakker's injury and the sudden concern about certain Superstars being shoved down the fans' throats.

Throw in the puzzling use of Breakker creatively when he finally returned from injury at WrestleMania, and you had a group that very much felt snakebitten and doomed to be one of the great "what ifs" in modern WWE history.

Then came the ongoing rivalry with Oba Femi and the revival of the once-prominent faction.

One thing is consistent in professional wrestling: if you book an individual or group to look like a megastar, they will be treated like one.

After months of wandering in the midcard, any star power or perceived main event aura The Vision previously had was extinguished by subpar booking. Enter Femi, fresh off a three-match series with the retiring Brock Lesnar that left zero doubt as to his place in the hierarchy of WWE Superstars.

The introduction of The Ruler's feud with Breakker instantly elevated the stature of The Vision. Pairing the group with this red-hot babyface, whom fans believed was a main event talent because of his work with Lesnar and the extent to which the future Hall of Famer put him over, instantly reintroduced them to the main event stratosphere.

Suddenly, Breakker, who had become a background player in the group he was expected to lead, was back at the forefront and in a position in which he belonged.

The faction's re-emergence as a top-tier player in WWE, and on the Raw brand, is not limited to its return to or near the top of the card. Two other key elements have significantly impacted the group's return to prominence and cannot be undervalued.

Do not underestimate the effect Maxxine Dupri's heel turn and alliance with The Faction have had on the group.

At one point this summer, The Vision felt like an afterthought. The group was a definitive midcard act that fans had stopped caring about. Anything special about them disappeared amid the injuries and less-than-effective booking that plagued the group.

Then came Dupri, whose mean, self-centered, deceitful turn injected the trio of bros with much-needed energy and gave the fans something to invest in. They booed the group mercilessly as they bullied the former Women's Intercontinental Champion's longtime teammates, Alpha Academy.

If Theory was the high school jock that fans loved to hate because of his unearned arrogance, she was his varsity cheerleader girlfriend who made him that much more insufferable.

She absolutely impacted the way fans saw that group and was the first building block necessary to elevate it back to relevance in WWE.

The latest return put it over the top and returned the much-needed main event aura to the group.

Bronson Reed's return and subsequent beatdown of Femi, including seven Tsunami splashes across Sunday Night's Main Event and the following evening's episode of Raw, did more to positively impact the way the audience views The Vision than anything.

The big man returned from injury and, ala Tazz (for about three weeks at the start of the new Millennium), the mood changed.

In the best shape of his career, the 2024 Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal winner was the shot of energy the group needed to be perceived as a top-tier act.

Perhaps it was the intensity and aggression with which he attacked Femi. Maybe it was the underrated aura that has always surrounded him, even when the creative team was more interested in his teammates. Whatever the case may be, his return and the manner in which he carried himself served as a major boost for The Vision and gave fans the impression that it could not believably combat Femi, but could also resume its main event-worthy run.

That does not mean it does not face hurdles on the Raw brand.

The Bloodline has been re-established in post-WrestleMania 42 WWE, and the new 946 faction headed by Royce Keys has made a large impact in a short time. That is the headline feud on the red brand right now and is expected to be for the foreseeable future, especially with Survivor Series: War Games coming up.

Luckily for The Vision, there is still the question of Paul Heyman's loyalties and the mystery surrounding the person who called him about the group's beatdown of Femi Monday night on Raw.

Who was it? Could it be the founder of the group, Rollins, potentially re-establishing a link to the group? Maybe it is a new, interested party ready to hitch their wagon to The Vision and carry it to ever greater success.

Whatever the case may be, the group is on the upswing and headed back to a position on the Raw brand that some thought it may never see again, and understandably so.

How WWE follows up its recent creative successes will ultimately determine if it is for good or a momentary flirtation with prominence.

articles.title: Penn State news: D'Anton Lynn celebrates 2026 squad for coming together
articles.summary: Penn State is 1-0 on the year with a 45-0 win over Marshall. Transfer quarterback Rocco Becht was great for Penn State, throwing for 271 yards and four touc...
articles.body:
Penn State is 1-0 on the year with a 45-0 win over Marshall. Transfer quarterback Rocco Becht was great for Penn State , throwing for 271 yards and four touchdowns.

Now, new defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn is talking about all of the transfers and how they have come together, per Allie Berubue of ABC27.

"I feel like we have a high level of trust on our defensive staff and that trickles down to the players," Lynn said. "It's to the point now, we're all Penn Staters now. You can't tell who's been here, you can't tell who is from Iowa State , who came from a different school. We're all Penn Staters now."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Overall, Penn State brought in 39 transfers. The Nittany Lions lost over 40 players after James Franklin left, but replaced them with a solid group. Over half of the transfers coming in came with Matt Campbell from Iowa State, including quarterback Rocco Becht . Meanwhile, Kenau Williams, Siale Taupaki, and Kyron Hudson joined the team from UCLA and USC, but all three of them had ties to Lynn at those two schools.

Lynn also brought with him a staff that came from all over, but is coming together as one .

"For me, it starts with the staff," Lynn said on Tuesday. "If you want a certain culture on your side of the football or the team, it starts with the staff. This is my third time with a new defensive staff and building a defense from scratch. The more you can make it our defense" — Lynn clasped his hands together, interlocking his 10 fingers — "the more everyone feels like they are a part of it."

articles.title: Denzel Ward purchases a stake in the Cleveland Guardians
articles.summary: Browns cornerback Denzel Ward signed a two-year contract extension this offseason and he's investing some of that money in another one of the city's sports t...
articles.body:
Browns cornerback Denzel Ward signed a two-year contract extension this offseason and he's investing some of that money in another one of the city's sports teams.

According to multiple reports, Ward has purchased a stake in the Cleveland Guardians. The Guardians are owned by Paul Dolan and David Blitzer with Blitzer in position to become the team's majority owner in the coming years.

Ward is not the only NFL player with a stake in the Guardians. Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is also a minority shareholder in the club and both players attended this year's home opener in Blitzer's suite.

Ward grew up outside of Cleveland and has spent his entire NFL career with the Browns. The investment in the Guardians suggests he'll remain tied to the city beyond his playing career as well.

articles.title: Juventus considers signing free agent to solve midfield emergency
articles.summary: Juventus are considering making a move for Marcelo Brozovic after losing Manuel Locatelli to injury for the rest of 2026, leaving the Bianconeri in need of c...
articles.body:
Juventus are considering making a move for Marcelo Brozovic after losing Manuel Locatelli to injury for the rest of 2026 , leaving the Bianconeri in need of cover in midfield.

Locatelli joins Khephren Thuram among the midfielders who will probably not play for the club until 2027 after both underwent surgery. Juve have also dealt with minor injuries to players such as Weston McKennie , further reducing their options in the position.

The Bianconeri are now just one major midfield injury away from a full-blown crisis, while the men at the Allianz Stadium cannot sign players under contract until the January transfer window opens.

This leaves Juve with limited options, but they can still make a move for free agents. That is what the Bianconeri are now trying to do, with Tuttomercatoweb claiming they are interested in Brozovic.

Brozovic is currently a free agent after his contract at Al Nassr was not renewed, while the former Inter Milan man wants to return to European football. The midfielder could represent an appealing option for Juventus given his experience and availability.

Another factor that could help Juve is Brozovic's previous relationship with Luciano Spalletti. The Bianconeri manager knows the midfielder very well, meaning he could be open to a reunion with the experienced player.

The midfielder has extensive experience in Italian football, which could make his adaptation to Juventus relatively straightforward if he can prove his fitness and prepare for competitive action quickly.

Juve need solutions in midfield after losing Locatelli and Thuram for extended periods, while McKennie's recent injury has also highlighted the lack of depth available to Spalletti.

Brozovic could therefore give the Bianconeri an experienced option at a time when their midfield is becoming increasingly stretched. His free agent status also gives Juventus an opportunity to strengthen before the January transfer window.

For Spalletti, the priority will be ensuring his midfield remains capable of handling the demands of the season. If Brozovic can regain his fitness quickly, he could become a useful solution to the problems currently facing the Bianconeri.

After months of waiting and the implementation of a new offensive system, the Philadelphia Eagles will open their season against the Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on Sept. 13. articles.title: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar: “The Clippers Pay For Kawhi And His Uncle’s Greed”
articles.summary: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar believes Kawhi Leonard escaped with relatively minor punishment while the Clippers lost five crucial first-round picks.
articles.body:
NBA legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar delivered a scathing assessment of the Los Angeles Clippers ' salary cap circumvention scandal , arguing that the franchise is ultimately paying the price for Kawhi Leonard and his uncle Dennis Robertson's actions.

Writing on his Substack, Kareem began with the importance of competitive fairness and explained that the salary cap only works if every franchise operates under the same rules and restrictions.

"Rules only work if they're the same for everyone. That's a fundamental principle in any sport. Take basketball: if one team gets two points for a layup and the other team gets three, it's pretty clear which team has the advantage. If one team has five players on the court and the other team has four, I know who I'm betting on. The salary cap works the same way. If I can pay my best player $50 million a year and you can only pay yours $40 million, chances are that the better player is going to want to play for me."

"That's the rule the Clippers and their owner Steve Ballmer were accused of violating with their star player Kawhi Leonard, and based on the investigation and report by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, it seems pretty clear that they were guilty as charged."

"This story has been hovering over the NBA for the past year, ever since the podcaster Pablo Torre reported that Leonard had signed a four-year, $28-million endorsement agreement with Aspiration Partners, an environmental startup that Ballmer had invested $50 million into just weeks earlier. According to Torre, Leonard did essentially nothing in return: no advertisements, no public appearances, no evidence he ever promoted the company in any way."

"A clause in the contract said it would be voided if Leonard ever left the team, making it seem all the more like part of his Clippers deal. Aspiration has since gone bankrupt and its founder has gone to jail for fraud, which probably explains why former employees were willing to talk to Torre and later the NBA's investigators. One former Aspiration executive told Torre point blank that Leonard's deal with the company was a way "to circumvent the salary cap."

"The big question, from the League's perspective, is: Who are the cheaters here? The Clippers, Ballmer, and his executives? Leonard? Leonard's uncle, Dennis Robertson, who negotiated his nephew's deals with both the team and the company? Based on the punishments handed out, it looks like the League is dividing the guilt between the team and Robertson, while giving Leonard a free pass. Ballmer, not surprisingly, denies doing anything wrong and says he's going to sue, but I'll believe that when I see it."

"Where to begin? The Clippers were hit with a $30 million fine, the biggest in NBA history, and they're losing five first-round draft picks over the next decade. In addition, Ballmer and team business president Gillian Zucker were suspended for a year, while basketball president Lawrence Frank was suspended for six months. Let's break that down. The $30 million the Clippers were fined amounts to 0.02 percent of Ballmer's $150 billion net worth. That's a percentage so small and a net worth so large that it's hard to put into perspective. So look at it like this: if you had one million dollars to your name, an equivalent fine would be two hundred bucks, or a pair of upper-level tickets and a couple of hot dogs and Cokes at a Clippers game."

"The real pain for Ballmer is not being able to watch a single minute of his team's games at the Intuit Dome, the $2 billion arena he paid for out of his own pocket, for the next year. People worth $150 billion aren't often told what they can and can't do, so that's a pretty big humiliation for the former Microsoft CEO. Meanwhile, Zucker and Frank are each losing their salary while they're suspended, which isn't going to put them in the poorhouse but probably genuinely hurts. And the organization is losing five first-round draft picks. Which means that the team Ballmer gets to watch (when he is allowed back into his arena) is not going to be as good as the one he hoped to watch when he first signed Kawhi—to say nothing of the fans."

"Robertson, meanwhile, has been banned from having any dealings with the NBA and all its teams for five years. For Uncle Dennis, as he is known in the press and throughout the League, that's about as bad as it can get. A five-year suspension will take him to Leonard's age-40 season, which makes it a de facto lifetime ban. After all, I don't think any other player is going to hire him as their representative after this fiasco. But, given that he is Leonard's uncle and has been his principal advisor since his father died while he was in high school, I imagine Leonard will continue to ensure he is provided for in the manner to which he is accustomed."

"Leonard, for his part, was fined $700,000, the amount of forbidden expenses he took directly from the Clippers. That's roughly what he makes to play in one NBA game. In other words, it's another case of relative chump change, especially when you consider that, according to the League's report, he actually collected $18 million in endorsement money from Aspiration and three other companies the Clippers introduced him to, and he did next to nothing in exchange for that money. That's on top of his $400 million in legitimate career earnings in the NBA."

"Leonard's official statement reinforces the notion that he was a victim in this case, not one of the perpetrators:

"Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap."

"If this whole thing feels like a giant whitewash to you, you're not alone. How exactly do you "accept full responsibility" while still blaming the whole thing on "people within my inner circle"? Leonard signed contracts with all those companies that were paying him money he wasn't allowed."

"And it was widely reported in 2019 that Uncle Dennis had previously solicited teams for all sorts of perks the League's collective bargaining agreement didn't permit, including an ownership stake in whatever team he signed with, a private jet at his disposal, and free housing, which probably doesn't mean a room at the Motel 6. He could have reined his uncle in then, or sent him packing, but instead he seems to have told him to find a better way to circumvent the cap. Does that sound like "integrity and respect" to you?"

"What it comes down to is that the League seems to have negotiated with the players' union to give Kawhi a slap on the wrist in exchange for the union not taking the case to arbitration. And now that the team is almost guaranteed to be terrible for the foreseeable future, thanks to all the draft picks they've lost, Kawhi is heading out of town, back to the Toronto Raptors , where he won a championship in 2019. So, in the end, the Clippers pay for Kawhi and his uncle's greed, while Ballmer has to spend the next year living the life of a guy with $150 billion who doesn't own an NBA team."

"The only real victims that I can find any sympathy for are the fans of this hapless organization. Since 1970, when they joined the League as the Buffalo Braves, they've never won a championship, or even made it to the NBA finals. Ballmer was supposed to be their savior, following the horrors of the Donald Sterling era. Kawhi was supposed to lead them to the promised land. But, considering the way things are going, the wait for a Clippers championship isn't likely to end anytime soon."

The NBA legend thinks that the investigation made it pretty clear that the Clippers were guilty of violating almost every principle.

The Clippers received a historic punishment , which included a $30 million fine, the loss of five first-round picks, and one-year suspensions for Steve Ballmer and business veteran Gillian Zucker, while Lawrence Frank got a six-month suspension.

But Abdul-Jabbar believes Leonard escaped with a very light punishment.

Kawhi Leonard was ordered to pay $700,000 in restitution after the investigation found that he had received over $18 million in endorsement agreements with Aspiration and three other companies .

The six-time champion was very doubtful of Leonard's statement after the investigation . Leonard said he had accepted full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people in his circle, as he maintained that he entered the agreements in good faith and had no knowledge of an attempt to circumvent the salary cap.

Kareem was not convinced, as he pointed to Robertson's history. He referenced reports from Leonard's 2019 free agency, when his uncle wanted benefits that were explicitly prohibited under the collective bargaining agreement, and questioned why Leonard allowed Robertson to continue handling his affairs afterward.

Ultimately, Kareem believes the Clippers and their fans have been left carrying the biggest consequences as Kawhi Leonard prepares to move on to the Toronto Raptors, as the trade is nearly finalized.

For Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Clippers fans are the only people in this entire scandal who deserve a little bit of sympathy. After decades without an NBA Finals appearance, they now face an uncertain future, and this time without five crucial first-round picks.

articles.title: How The Hornets Could Land Domantas Sabonis As Rumors Heat Up
articles.summary: With trade rumors surrounding Domantas Sabonis gathering more traction, we explore how the Hornets could acquire him.
articles.body:
It is a well-known fact that the Sacramento Kings have been gearing up for a rebuild. While this is a promising sign for a team that has struggled to perform, offloading the contracts of Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine has delayed the process.

As things stand, there appears to be no way for Sacramento to part with LaVine, whose trade value seems to be at an all-time low. However, with rumors suggesting that Domantas Sabonis could demand a trade in the near future , there may be some hope.

Surprisingly, a suitor may have an eye on the Lithuanian big man. According to NBA insider Jake Fischer , the Charlotte Hornets could be interested in the Kings' star. While addressing the rumors involving Domantas Sabonis , Fischer shed more light on the situation, stating:

"Domantas Sabonis is also going to want an extension. He had trade interest from Toronto. He had trade interest from Charlotte. Both teams, I believe, were in discussions with Sacramento about him as recently as this summer."

"I think Toronto's trade talks with the Kings were far more focused and serious back in February, before the trade deadline. But Charlotte, I think, is a team that could still be in the mix for him depending on Sacramento's price point."

Fischer emphasized that the Kings were looking for "positive trade value" in return for Domantas Sabonis. While he also noted that there may not be many teams that could view his $45.4 million cap hit as positive, the Hornets may be in a favorable position compared to other franchises.

In light of this, here is a potential trade package that would allow Charlotte to acquire Domantas Sabonis:

Charlotte Hornets Receive: Domantas Sabonis

Sacramento Kings Receive: Grayson Allen , Grant Williams , Ryan Kalkbrenner , 2029 first-round pick (MIN swap), 2033 (PHX)

Financially, this trade scenario is quite intriguing. Although Sabonis' $45.4 million contract is far greater than the combined incoming cap hit of $34.3 million from Charlotte, the Hornets have a massive $40.7 million trade exception from the LaMelo Ball trade. Thus, absorbing the additional $11.1 million in salary would not be an issue for the Hornets.

Thus, with the fiscal aspect satisfied, we look at how this trade would impact each team.

How Do The Kings Benefit From This Trade?

The Kings' desire to gain positive trade value from Domantas Sabonis' contract creates some challenges. However, Charlotte's offer could be viewed quite favorably.

Other than the two first-round picks, Sacramento would acquire two reliable veterans in Grayson Allen and Grant Williams , along with a promising young center in Ryan Kalkbrenner .

Allen ($18.1 million) and Williams ($14.2 million) have immense value from a contract perspective. Although Allen has a $19.3 million player option, Williams is on an expiring contract. This would allow Sacramento to free up at least $14.2 million in cap space next summer.

In terms of performance, both veterans also have a lot to offer. At 31, Allen remains an elite perimeter shooter and a solid wing defender. With averages of 16.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.4 steals per game while shooting 40.3% from the field and 34.9% from three-point range, he could be a solid bench player for the Kings.

Meanwhile, Williams is also impactful. As a versatile defender against larger players, Williams could be a reliable small-ball center in Sacramento's rotation. When you also factor in last season's averages of 7.0 points, 3.9 rebounds, 0.5 steals, and 0.5 blocks per game on 38.8% shooting from beyond the arc, his ability to space the floor may also have value.

While parting with a big man like Domantas Sabonis could be difficult, it allows the Kings to give Maxime Raynaud a larger role. Hence, to support Raynaud, Sacramento could use Ryan Kalkbrenner, who averaged 7.6 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game as a key player in the Hornets' rotation.

Although this trade would see several players join Sacramento's roster, the blend of veteran experience and young talent could be worthwhile.

How Does Domantas Sabonis' Addition Help The Hornets?

The Charlotte Hornets will be one of the NBA's most interesting teams entering the 2026-27 season. After parting ways with LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges , the Hornets have changed course. Now, with a new core powering the team, the Hornets could be worth keeping an eye on.

Currently, Charlotte has a solid frontcourt rotation anchored by Naz Reid . However, adding a legitimate center in Domantas Sabonis would give Reid the flexibility to play at the 4, making him a far greater threat.

Needless to say, Sabonis is noteworthy in his own right. Although he was limited to making only 19 appearances last season, the Lithuanian averaged 15.8 points, 11.4 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game. Given his career averages of 16.1 points, 10.1 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game, the Hornets could look to Sabonis as a reliable presence on the glass and a remarkable playmaker in the post.

Given the Hornets' roster makeup, Sabonis would not need to anchor the offense. In many ways, giving him the freedom to contribute with his rebounding and innate playmaking could transform Charlotte into a more formidable unit.

Should The Hornets Trade For Domantas Sabonis?

For obvious reasons, the trade proposal above is hypothetical, but given the upsides of landing Domantas Sabonis, the Charlotte Hornets would be urged to pull the trigger on a deal. However, the team would be advised to be mindful of the big man's contract.

As Fischer mentioned, Sabonis is eligible for an extension this summer. While he still has another year left on his contract, players have shown an inclination to sign new deals before risking unrestricted free agency.

Currently, the Hornets are in a favorable position to acquire Sabonis owing to their massive trade player exception. However, if they choose to offer Domantas Sabonis a long-term extension, it could hurt their chances of retaining key players like Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel in the future.

The perils of the second apron should not be overlooked in such scenarios. Hence, considering how important it is for Charlotte to build around Miller and Knueppel, the team must exercise caution if they enter negotiations with the Kings.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals depth chart: 6 week 1 observations
articles.summary: The Cardinals released their first depth chart of 2026. These are some things of note.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals prepare to face the Los Angeles Chargers this week in their season opener. As part of that, they released their first depth chart of the year. Most of it was as expected, but there were a few things of note.

The quarterback situation is as expected. The starting offensive line was as expected, but there are a few things to note.

Love, the third overall pick in the draft, is not the Cardinals' starting running back. That title belongs to Tyler Allgeier , signed in the offseason in free agency. This is something in name only, as both will have significant roles in the offense. But it is interesting to see that one of the most highly touted players in the draft is going to be on the bench instead of starting.

Jeremiyah Love, Max Melton as kick returners

Love had a few kick return reps at the very beginning of OTAs. He didn't do it in training camp and didn't do it in the preseason. However, he is listed as the third kick returner behind Devin Duvernay and Max Melton. Melton also hasn't returned any kicks in the NFL.

It is weird because the Cardinals also have running back Bam Knight and receiver Jalen Brooks , both of whomo have experience returninig kicks.

As expected, Jack Gibbens is listed as the starter alongside Mack Wilson . Cody Simon is listed behind Wilson as the backup "Mike." He will likely get some snaps in the defensive rotation, though.

Robinson, a former first-round pick, is not a starter. Dante Stills is listed ahead of him at left defensive tackle.

Both are listed with an or between them as a starting outside linebacker opposite Josh Sweat . This was the case for much of last season, too.

Andrew Wingard is the starting free safety, replacing Jalen Thompson . Rabbit Taylor-Demerson will be the No. 3 safety as he was last season. He is listed as the No. 2 strong safety behind Budda Baker .
